Job Description:

Business Development Representative (Commercial Branding and Transportation)


Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.


This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.


The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

As a Business Development Representative, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:


  • Selling 3M CBT products, specifying 3M solutions to drive growth within key accounts
  • Building relationships with key account sales teams, training on 3M solutions, new account prospecting, vetting, onboarding, activation, resulting in accelerated sales growth.
  • Coordinate new business development efforts with Sales Management, Portfolio Teams (APL’s, CDM’s), Shopper Marketing, Sales Operations, Finance, Business Analytics, Application Engineers and Supply Chain.
  • Develop relationships with key stakeholders both external and internal. Top down, bottom up, inside out approach.
  • Properly manage sales estimates, CIP, MDF, rebates, claims, travel budgets.
  • Interpreting industry trends, customer requirements, and business objectives to define guidelines/methods to achieve sales targets.

Company Vehicle

This position requires driving a company vehicle, which will require pre-employment and ongoing review of motor vehicle history for candidates who are offered and hired for this position.


Your Skills and Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:


  • Bachelor’s degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)
  • Five (5) years of sales experience with account management responsibility in a retail, private, public, government or military environment.
  • Current, valid Driver’s License.

Additional qualifications that will help you succeed even further in this role include:


  • Ten (10) + years experience in sales with a combination of key account and brands.
  • Experience with Brand Owners and developing a sales pipeline on Brand projects
  • Key Account Management experience
  • Strong work ethic. Willingness to go the extra mile. Proven track record of success.
  • Self-starter with positive mental attitude who follows up and follows through.
  • Advance leadership and project management skills.
  • Independent and strategic thinker able to make solid business decisions.
  • Ability to analyze and apply data to drive strategy and sales.
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills for interacting with team members, customers, and division management.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Energized by fast paced, challenging work environment.
  • Experience working with digital marketing tactics, e-commerce, & AI.
  • Expertise with Sales Force, Power BI, Workday, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint.
  • Willingness to make the call. Relentless approach to developing new business for 3M.

Work location: This role follows a remote working model.

Travel: May include up to 50% domestic/international

Relocation: Not included


Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).


Supporting Your Well-being

3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.


Chat with Max

For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers.

Applicable to US Applicants Only:The expected compensation range for this position is $145,676 - $178,049, which includes base pay plus variable incentive pay, if eligible. This range represents a good faith estimate for this position. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s relevant knowledge, training, skills, work location, and/or experience. In addition, this position may be eligible for a range of benefits (e.g., Medical, Dental & Vision, Health Savings Accounts, Health Care & Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Disability Benefits, Life Insurance, Voluntary Benefits, Paid Absences and Retirement Benefits, etc.). This agreement lays out key terms on using 3M Confidential Information and Trade Secrets. It also has provisions discussing conflicts of interest and how inventions are assigned. jobs.title: Crux - Video and Audio QA - English (US)
jobs.excerpt: Overview We are hiring Quality Control (QC) evaluators for a project that spans both Search and Linguistic tasks.
jobs.description:
Overview

We are hiring Quality Control (QC) evaluators for a project that spans both Search and Linguistic tasks. You will perform quality checks on initial ratings produced by evaluators—validating user intent assessment, query annotation, text classification, and multimedia (video, image, audio) reviews for relevanc, accuracy, and guideline adherence. The ideal candidate combines strong language skills with sharp analytical judgment, excellent documentation and feedback skills, and familiarity with short-form video culture.

What you will do

  • Audit samples of initial ratings for relevance, intent alignment, taxonomy compliance, and linguistic quality.
  • Re-rate items (double-scoring) to verify labels; resolve discrepancies and document decisions.
  • Perform linguistic quality checks (grammar, tone, clarity, local relevance) and media comprehension reviews.
  • Classify and track errors using an agreed error taxonomy; surface trends and edge cases.
  • Provide clear, actionable feedback to evaluators; contribute to guideline clarifications and updates.
  • Participate in and lead calibration sessions to drive inter-rater agreement.
  • Track and report QC metrics (e.g., agreement rates, accuracy, error trends) and meet QC SLAs.
  • Triage escalations, handle ambiguous cases, and ensure data integrity and compliance.
  • Use internal tools to complete, track, and submit QC tasks accurately.

Project Details

    Engagement Type: Freelance

    Rate: USD 28.61/hour

    Estimated Hours: 15-30 hours/week

Requirement

  • Native or near-native speaker level in English language with strong reading, writing, and listening comprehension.
  • Excellent grammar, writing, and proofreading skills.
  • Strong video and image comprehension; good hearing ability for audio tasks.
  • Solid understanding of search engines, user intent, and web content.
  • High attention to detail, consistency, and guideline adherence.
  • Ability to deliver clear written feedback and rationale.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in QC/QA for text classification, query annotation, data labeling, or search quality evaluation.
  • Familiarity with short dramas and local short-drama culture/platforms.
  • Experience with calibrations, sampling, scorecards, and root-cause analysis.
  • Comfortable working with productivity and quality targets; proficient with spreadsheets/QA tools.
  • Background in linguistics, communications, media studies, information science, or related field.

jobs.title: Merchandising Specialist II
jobs.excerpt: About ePromos ePromos Promotional Products, LLC, has been a leading industry distributor in the promotional space for over 20 years!
jobs.description:
About ePromos
ePromos Promotional Products, LLC, has been a leading industry distributor in the promotional space for over 20 years! Our award-winning website combined with our sales strategy, service capabilities and enterprise level solutions consistently set us apart.

As a remote-first company, ePromos embraces flexibility, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Our team is composed of passionate professionals who thrive in a fast-paced, performance-driven culture where ideas are valued and innovation is encouraged. Our values are strong with a deep-rooted emphasis on giving back as part of our ePromos Cares mission.

At ePromos, we don’t just sell products—we help build brands. Join us and be part of a company that’s redefining the promotional marketing space through strategic thinking, bold creativity, and a people-first approach.

BASIC FUNCTION SUMMARY:
The Merchandising Specialist II is responsible for managing the execution and ongoing optimization of assigned corporate client merchandising programs within the promotional products industry. This role partners closely with the Sourcing & Merchandising Manager, Program Account Managers, and cross-functional teams to source products, develop curated assortments, analyze program performance, and deliver strategic client-ready merchandising recommendations.

This position requires hands-on experience in the promotional products industry and a strong understanding of sourcing processes, supplier capabilities, decoration methods, and production timelines. The ideal candidate combines analytical thinking with strong product knowledge, sound professional judgment, and the ability to independently manage multiple client programs and lead merchandising discussions in a fast-paced, client-facing environment.

This position is open to remote candidates throughout the United States, with a preference for candidates based in the Greater Cincinnati area. Local candidates will be expected to work in a hybrid capacity at our Fairfield, Ohio warehouse approximately 2–3 days per week, with flexibility based on business needs and scheduled client visits.

The following duties are not intended to serve as a comprehensive list of all duties required for this position. The job description is a summary of the major duties and responsibilities. This role may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be expected to perform additional duties as requested.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Duties, Skills, Responsibilities, and Expectations
Account Management, Reporting & Analysis
  • Manage the merchandising activities and ongoing optimization of assigned client programs, partnering with Program Account Managers to align recommendations with client goals, brand standards, timelines, and business objectives.
  • Prepare and maintain recurring sales velocity reports, SKU scorecards, and performance summaries to monitor program health and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Analyze SKU performance, sell-through, margins, and engagement data to develop actionable recommendations that improve assortment productivity, product relevance, and program profitability.
  • Monitor Google Analytics and other engagement data to identify trends and recommend improvements to product assortments, merchandising placement, and program engagement.
  • Conduct carbon footprint reporting as required by client programs (quarterly, annually, or ad hoc).
  • Exercise independent judgment in day-to-day merchandising decisions, escalating significant strategic, financial, or operational matters to the Sourcing & Merchandising Manager for review and approval.
Product Sourcing and Assortment Planning
  • Manage assigned client sourcing requests, including one-off product needs, assortment refreshes, and Limited Time Buys (LTBs), in accordance with established sourcing protocols and service-level expectations.
  • Develop and recommend customized product assortment strategies that align with client brand guidelines, budget parameters, margin targets, target audiences, and program objectives.
  • Source products by working directly with suppliers, evaluating product availability, decoration capabilities, pricing, and production timelines.
  • Develop accurate product pricing and client-ready sourcing recommendations, including product specifications, decoration options, lead times, and cost details.
Inventory, SKU and Program Management
  • Evaluate SKU expansion requests based on program capacity, operational feasibility, and anticipated performance impact.
  • Proactively identify underperforming SKUs and recommend promotional strategies, product substitutions, assortment adjustments, or phase-outs.
  • Analyze inventory levels, SKU performance, and replenishment trends to identify risks and recommend inventory adjustments in partnership with Program Account Managers and internal stakeholders.
  • Track project timelines and proactively identify and communicate sourcing, production, inventory, or fulfillment risks, recommending solutions as appropriate.
Trend Analysis and Merchandising Strategy
  • Utilize internal systems (e.g., NetSuite) and external market sources to identify emerging categories, product, and consumer trends.
  • Apply trend insights to assortment planning, product refresh cycles, and new program launches to ensure merchandise offerings remain relevant and competitive.
  • Contribute strategic merchandising insights and recommendations to support program optimization, assortment innovation, and continuous improvement within the Sourcing & Merchandising department.
Client Interaction and Communication
  • Independently lead client merchandising discussions, present strategic product recommendations, and collaborate with Program Account Managers to support client objectives.
  • Serve as a merchandising subject-matter expert, providing thoughtful, solution-oriented product recommendations and guidance.
  • Develop and deliver high-quality client presentations that clearly communicate assortment strategies, product recommendations, and relevant trade-offs.
  • Document key decisions, feedback, and action items from client and internal meetings, ensuring timely follow-up and communication with stakeholders.
  • Build credibility and trust with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and clients through clear, accurate, and professional communication.
New Store Implementations
  • Lead assigned merchandising workstreams for new client store implementations, including product sourcing, assortment development, pricing coordination, and milestone management.
  • Develop data-informed assortment recommendations that align with client goals, brand guidelines, target audiences, budget parameters, and program requirements.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Implementation, Creative, and other internal stakeholders to support successful program launches.
  • Lead merchandising discussions during client implementation meetings, communicate assortment strategies, document client feedback, and coordinate revisions to support timely program launches.
Additional Responsibilities – Fairfield Cincinnati-Based Employees
In addition to the core Merchandising Specialist II responsibilities, Cincinnati-based employees will support the following activities:
  • Partner with the Sourcing & Merchandising team to maintain and update the warehouse showroom, ensuring product displays remain aligned with the Essentials Marketplace assortment, including adding new products and removing discontinued or retired items.
  • Coordinate and execute showroom display updates ahead of client visits, highlighting products and merchandising solutions tailored to specific client needs and opportunities.
  • Actively participate in client showroom visits and meetings, partnering with Sales to present product recommendations, showcase in-house decoration capabilities, and communicate the strategic merchandising solutions and expertise available through the Sourcing & Merchandising team.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of the warehouse's existing and evolving in-house decoration capabilities, including decoration methods, equipment, and production considerations. Proactively collaborate with warehouse personnel to stay informed of new capabilities and identify opportunities to incorporate these offerings into client merchandising recommendations.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
  • Bachelor's degree in Merchandising, Marketing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated experience sourcing and merchandising products for client programs or e-commerce stores.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, including the ability to independently develop Excel-based reports, analyze data, and create professional, client-facing presentations.
  • Working knowledge of NetSuite or similar ERP/CRM systems; experience with Google Analytics or other e-commerce analytics tools preferred.
  • Strong understanding of promotional product decoration methods, supplier capabilities, and production timelines.
  • Ability to independently manage multiple client programs and projects in a deadline-driven environment.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to consistently follow through on commitments.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to confidently present recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, develop independent merchandising recommendations, and communicate trade-offs while recognizing when leadership escalation is appropriate.
PREFERRED SKILLS
  • 3+ years of experience in the promotional products industry, including distributor, agency, or supplier environments.
  • Experience with Jira or similar project management and workflow systems.
  • Strong analytical thinking and data-driven decision-making skills.
  • Experience with product assortment planning, SKU optimization, and merchandise performance analysis.
  • Strong project management and prioritization skills.
  • Experience leading client-facing merchandising discussions and presentations.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with suppliers and cross-functional teams.
  • Initiative, ownership, professional judgment, and adaptability in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
WORKING CONDITIONS:
  • Remote Eligible (U.S. Only) | Fairfield (Greater Cincinnati Area - Hybrid Preferred)
  • Cincinnati-based employees are expected to work a hybrid schedule at the local warehouse approximately 2–3 days per week, with flexibility based on business needs and scheduled client visits.
  • Occasional travel may be required based on client and business needs.
  • Ability to accommodate multiple time zones, with primary ET (EST/EDT) coverage
  • Dedicated workspace and high-speed internet required
  • Frequent video conference/email/chat communication
PHYSICAL DEMANDS
  • Maintaining a stationary position for up to 50% of the workday
  • Consistently operate a computer and other productivity equipment
  • Clarity of vision of 30” or less
  • Exertion of up to 10 lbs. for lifting or moving objects
  • For Cincinnati-based employees, occasional standing, walking, and handling of product samples or showroom displays may be required.
The base salary range for this role is $50,000-$65,000 per year. Compensation for this role will vary based on factors such as qualifications, experience, skill level, and competencies. The Company will meet minimum wage or the minimum of the pay range (whichever is higher) based on city, county, and state requirements.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer!
ePromos is committed to creating a diverse workplace environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status

We do not accept resume submissions from third party recruiters.

jobs.excerpt: 📋 Tasks and responsibilitiesData Management and Governance LeadThe Data Management and Governance Lead positions data as a strategic enterprise asset.
jobs.description:
📋 Tasks and responsibilities

Data Management and Governance Lead

The Data Management and Governance Lead positions data as a strategic enterprise asset. The role sets direction for data vision, strategy, governance, quality and data culture, ensuring that data supports operational efficiency, business value creation and regulatory compliance throughout the data lifecycle.

The role is responsible for designing, operationalizing and continuously evolving the enterprise data governance and data management framework in line with the organization’s data strategy and regulatory obligations.

As a strategic partner to the business, the Data Management and Governance Lead connects executive-level data ambitions with domain-level implementation through governance bodies, standards, tooling and change management.

The role also shapes the data strategy and roadmap, driving continuous improvement in data management practices.

🛠️ Your responsibilities

As Data Management and Governance Lead, your responsibilities will include:

1. Enterprise data governance leadership

  • Define, maintain and evolve the enterprise data governance framework, including policies, standards and roles.
  • Operationalize data ownership, data stewardship and accountability models across data domains.
  • Steer Data Governance Councils and working groups, ensuring effective decision-making.
  • Act as a reference point for data governance best practices.

2. Data strategy and roadmap ownership

  • Contribute directly to the definition and evolution of the enterprise data strategy.
  • Translate strategic data ambitions into a clear data governance and data management roadmap aligned with business priorities and platform evolution.
  • Track progress and maturity against strategic objectives, and report insights to the business.

3. Data quality and trust at scale

  • Design and deploy data quality frameworks, KPIs, KRIs and monitoring dashboards.
  • Drive the automation of data quality controls and governance workflows.
  • Oversee data quality issue management from identification through to remediation.
  • Ensure that data is fit for regulatory reporting, analytics and AI use cases.

4. Regulatory and risk alignment

  • Ensure that data governance and data management practices support regulatory compliance, including GDPR and Solvency II, as well as auditability and traceability.
  • Identify and assess data-related risks.
  • Embed governance controls into data processes to reduce risks.

5. Data culture and enablement

  • Promote data literacy, governance awareness and a quality mindset across the organization.
  • Coach Data Owners and Data Stewards.

jobs.description:
Description

About Sygnia
Sygnia is a leading global cyber readiness and incident response firm. Our teams operate on the digital frontlines of today’s most sophisticated cyber battles, helping the world’s top organizations withstand and recover from complex attacks, often in high-pressure, high-stakes environments. We combine technical excellence, elite talent, and battle-tested methodologies to help our clients build resilience and respond with confidence.

Sygnia is rapidly expanding its presence in the United States, growing our incident response capabilities and client base across key industries. Joining now means playing a formative role in shaping our U.S. operations while benefiting from the backing and expertise of an established global leader.

The Role
We’re seeking a highly technical and client-facing Incident Response Team Lead to spearhead incident response engagements and guide a small team of Incident Response Experts through some of the most challenging investigations in the industry. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in the trenches conducting deep technical investigations, leading response efforts, and serving as a trusted advisor to Fortune 500 security teams.

As a Team Lead, you will manage 2–5 direct reports, contribute hands-on to forensic and incident response work, and play a key role in building and refining our internal processes, tools, and methodologies. You’ll face ransomware and advanced threat actors head-on, helping our clients recover and emerge more secure than before.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead incident response investigations across a wide range of attack types, supporting organizations through both immediate response and longer-term remediation efforts.
  • Serve as the primary technical and advisory point of contact for internal and external security and IT teams.
  • Manage and mentor a small team of elite incident responders, supporting their growth and ensuring operational excellence.
  • Perform hands-on forensic analysis of systems, networks, and logs to identify indicators of compromise, persistence mechanisms, and lateral movement.
  • Leverage Sygnia’s internal tools and methodologies to guide containment, eradication, and recovery efforts.
  • Support threat hunting activities during and after engagements to identify residual attacker presence or undiscovered impact.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of Sygnia’s IR playbooks, detection and investigation processes, and internal tools.
  • Help scope new engagements, balancing client urgency with technical feasibility and team bandwidth.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • 3+ years of experience leading technical teams, with the ability to motivate, guide, and develop junior and mid-level talent.
  • Strong, demonstrable expertise in incident response, digital forensics, and malware or threat analysis.
  • Hands-on skills in analyzing host-based artifacts (Windows, Linux, macOS), log data, network captures, and disk/memory images.
  • Familiarity with attacker tradecraft, including lateral movement, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, and ransomware operations.
  • Experience working with enterprise environments and interacting directly with clients in high-pressure situations.
  • Strong communication skills, able to explain complex findings to both technical teams and executive stakeholders.
  • Experience in consulting or professional services environments is strongly preferred.
  • Knowledge of cloud forensics (AWS, Azure, GCP) or EDR platforms is a plus.
  • Ability to travel as needed (~25%) based on client engagements, sometimes with limited notice.

Bonus Points For

  • Industry-recognized certifications (e.g., GCFA, GCIH, GNFA, GCIA, GREM, CISSP).
  • Experience responding to ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), and advanced threat actor incidents.
  • Experience presenting findings to legal counsel, regulators, or board-level stakeholders.
  • Multilingual skills and experience in multinational or cross-cultural environments.
  • A degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field; or equivalent education or training in cybersecurity

Why Sygnia

  • Work with some of the best minds in cybersecurity on the world’s most high-impact cases.
  • Operate in a fast-paced, elite-tier environment where your technical expertise is trusted and valued.
  • Take part in meaningful, challenging work that directly shapes the outcomes for Fortune 500 organizations.
  • Grow your career while staying hands-on in incident response and mentoring a highly capable team.

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit to learn more.

About the role

Every device we ship starts with a forecast. We're hiring a Director to own how we forecast product demand, from the topline view of the business down to the units we need to build and stock. This is a senior, hands-on role for a sharp, curious problem solver. Our data is rich but complex, spread across many systems and broken down by product, region, channel, and customer segment. Both new products and existing products entering new markets launch with little or no history. You'll set the strategy and do the work yourself, using AI and automation to get the reach that would normally take a team. You'll be the senior forecasting partner to Finance, Sales, Product, and Supply Chain leadership, and your numbers will drive what we build, buy, and stock. You don't need to be a supply chain expert. We care more about how you think than about years spent in operations. If you're strong at forecasting, great with complex data, and learn fast, we'll help you learn the supply chain side.

What you'll do

  • Own the topline product forecast. Build and be accountable for the forecast by product line, connecting pipeline, bookings, and subscription trends to the hardware units those deals require.
  • Set the forecasting strategy. Define how we forecast and plan across the company: the process, cadence, systems, and tooling roadmap (including connected planning platforms such as Pigment).
  • Forecast new product introductions. Own launch forecasts for products with no sales history, using analogs, pipeline signals, pricing, and adoption assumptions. Plan cannibalization, transitions from legacy products, and end-of-life ramps.
  • Forecast every product in every market. Build forecasts for each product as it enters new geographies and segments, where adoption curves, pricing, sales channels, competition, and regulatory requirements can differ sharply from markets we already know. Decide when to borrow from established markets and when local signals should take over.
  • Translate forecast into unit demand. Break the topline down accurately by SKU, region, and channel, and keep it current as the business changes.
  • Connect complex data into one view. Bring together detailed data from multiple systems (CRM, ERP, shipments, activations) into a consistent picture of demand. Partner with data and systems owners to strengthen how that data flows into forecasting.
  • Scale with automation. Build repeatable pipelines, scripts, and AI-driven workflows so the forecast refreshes quickly and reliably as the business grows.
  • Turn demand into inventory plans. Partner with Supply Chain on build plans, safety stock, and weeks-of-supply targets, balancing the cost of running out against the cost of holding too much.
  • Lead the monthly demand review. Present scenarios, risks, and assumption changes to executives, and drive alignment on a single demand plan.
  • Own forecast performance. Set accuracy and bias targets, report on them, explain misses, and keep improving the process.

What you need

  • 8+ years in forecasting, demand planning, FP&A, analytics, or a similar quantitative role.
  • You pick up new business models and processes quickly and are energized by figuring out how things work.
  • Skill with complex, disaggregated data. A track record of pulling together detailed data from multiple sources, reconciling it at different levels of granularity, and turning it into forecasts leaders trust.
  • Strong SQL or a comparable tool. You've built processes that run without manual rebuilding each cycle.
  • Experience forecasting new products or new markets where history is thin, choosing sensible analogs, and adjusting quickly as real launch data comes in.
  • You use AI tools (LLMs, coding assistants, agents) every day as your default way of working: to write and debug code, clean data, build models, and draft analysis. You can show concrete examples of work AI made faster or better, and you know how to check AI output before trusting it.
  • You understand concepts like lead times, safety stock, and inventory levels, even if you haven't worked in supply chain directly.
  • You've owned an important process end to end and driven decisions across teams without formal authority.
  • You can explain a forecast, its assumptions, and its risks to senior leadership in plain language and defend it under pushback.

Nice to have

  • Hands-on experience with Pigment (or another connected planning tool such as Anaplan or Adaptive Planning).
  • Experience in a SaaS business: subscriptions, ARR, attach rates, and how bookings translate into device shipments.
  • Prior new product forecasting at a hardware + software company, including launch ramps and legacy product transitions.
  • Experience forecasting international or new-market expansion, where each region has its own adoption pattern, channels, and requirements.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: You understand our products, data sources, and current forecast process. You have a documented baseline forecast, a clear map of the data that feeds it, and a forecasting roadmap agreed with leadership.
  • First 6 months: The monthly demand review runs on a repeatable, largely automated process, and forecast accuracy and bias are reported regularly.
  • First year: Leadership and Supply Chain trust the forecast to drive build and inventory decisions. New products and new-market launches each start with a clear demand plan, accuracy is measurably improving, and the process is highly automated and scales with the business.
Pay Transparency

Job Description

RMI is seeking a Senior Associate who is motivated to tackle the issue of growing extreme heat stress by delivering efficient, affordable, lower climate impact cooling globally. We strongly encourage individuals from underrepresented groups to apply.

Program Overview

RMI's Buildings Program works to transform residential and commercial buildings to improve energy efficiency and comfort, accelerate electrification, reduce embodied carbon, and support a low-carbon electric grid. Our team supports regulatory and policy change, innovative market strategies, and new technology development and adoption, all to reduce emissions while improving affordability, resilience, health, and economic outcomes.

In India, the built environment programme works specifically to accelerate the transition to thermally comfortable, affordable, and low-carbon residential buildings. This includes reducing exposure to heat through urban and passive cooling strategies, improving building design and materials, and ensuring that when mechanical cooling is needed, it is efficient, affordable and climate friendly. The work combines applied research, pilot demonstrations, and programme implementation to generate actionable evidence for policy and market transformation.

Furthermore, whether in India or globally, Cooling (mainly active) is becoming an essential part of modern life as heat stress intensifies, populations urbanize, and demand for air conditioning and other cooling services grows rapidly. Delivering cooling at scale, however, requires more than improving individual technologies. It requires an integrated approach that can provide thermal comfort and protection from heat while keeping energy use, costs, grid impacts, and climate emissions from refrigerants and electricity sue manageable.

RMI’s cooling work brings together this whole systems perspective across three interconnected areas: reducing cooling demand and exposure through urban heat mitigation strategies and passive solutions; delivering cooling more efficiently through smarter technologies and breakthrough innovations; and reducing the climate impact of cooling through improved refrigerant choices and lifecycle management. The team works across geographies, combining research and market intelligence with technology assessment, field demonstrations, industry engagement, policy support, and market shaping strategies.

Position Overview:

RMI is seeking a highly motivated professional to contribute to its growing portfolio of work on thermal comfort and cooling. The individual will work across relevant initiatives in US, India, and globally, supporting efforts spanning energy-efficient air conditioning and refrigerant management, as well as urban heat mitigation, passive strategies, and emerging cooling technologies.

This role combines research and analysis with technical assessment, field engagement, and market and policy transformation. The individual will conduct research and develop analytical insights, support technology and market landscape assessments, participate in field validation studies, demonstrations and pilots, and translate lessons into practical, scalable solution as well as communicate these through compelling thought leadership pieces and presentations. The role will involve collaboration across RMI teams and external partners and will require periodic domestic and international travel.

Core Responsibilities

  • Research and analysis
    • Conduct quantitative and market research on technologies, markets, policies, standards, economics, and deployment pathways.
    • Develop technical subject matter knowledge of urban heat mitigation, passive strategies, active cooling solutions, refrigerants to engage credibly with stakeholders.
    • Translate the research into insights and recommendations.
    • Assess opportunities and develop strategies that allow solutions to scale in the market based on practical ground and institutional realities.
  • Field and market engagement
    • Participate in field visits to assess how technologies and systems operate in practice.
    • Support pilot activities, including technical specification, partner coordination, implementation tracking, and performance assessment, and translate field observations and stakeholder inputs into practical recommendations.
    • Support/Lead the planning and facilitation of workshops, roundtables, working sessions, and stakeholder consultations.
    • Support internal and external partners during in-person engagements with companies, governments, developers, communities, and other stakeholders to understand needs, constraints, and opportunities.
    • Work with technical partners to collect and analyze pilot data on thermal comfort, energy use, costs and emissions, as relevant to each intervention, and develop evidence-based case studies and business cases for wider adoption.
  • Communications
    • Communicate and collaborate across programs and geographies within RMI through internal memos, calls, and presentations
    • Write clear, compelling reports, briefs, presentations, articles, and any other external facing materials.
    • Contribute to communications and outreach that build awareness on the issue of heat and suitable cooling solutions among policymakers, industry, practitioners, and consumers.
  • Project Management
    • Manage assigned workplans, timelines, deliverables, budgets, and internal coordination using RMI’s project management tools and processes.
    • Coordinate with project team to identify risks, track grant milestones and outcomes, and ensure timely delivery of project outputs and funder reports.
    • Support with drafting concept notes, proposals, and any funder-facing materials.
    • Support management of contractors and advisors.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional experience in the energy, sustainability, built environment or related sector, with a preference for background or expertise in energy efficiency, building design strategies, and cooling & heating energy systems.
  • Undergraduate degree in engineering (mechanical, chemical preferred), environmental science, building science, or a related discipline.
  • Strong technical and policy research and analytical skills, as well as written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • Ability to work independently while being a strong team player with excellent interpersonal/collaborative skills with staff and counterparts at all organizational levels and with external partners.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters degree in engineering (mechanical, chemical preferred), environmental science, building science, or a related discipline.
  • Experience working with manufacturers, contractors, vendors, researchers, and end users of cooling equipment, refrigerants, and related solutions
  • Background working directly with senior-level stakeholders from industry, finance, or other areas, especially relating to energy/emissions goals.
  • Experience with group facilitation and producing powerful insights from workshops and convenings.

Visa Sponsorship

Please note: At this time, RMI is not able to sponsor employment visas or hire candidates who require visa sponsorship to work in the United States. All candidates must have current, independent authorization to work in the U.S. without present or future sponsorship from RMI. We will update our hiring pages if this status changes.


Location   

This role can be located from anywhere in the United States or Europe. Domestic and international travel is expected to and within India and other target geographies, subject to discussion and approval by senior leadership.

We provide you with the essential IT equipment plus a one-time home technology payment and a monthly work from home/commuter allowance to ensure you have a comfortable home office set up and necessary supplies.

We love seeing each other in person! We occasionally gather for shared time together like retreats and learning experiences. Be ready to travel for occasional in-person meetings (and of course, we cover travel costs).

Compensation 

At RMI, we prioritize fairness in our pay practices. Salaries are determined based on a mix of experience, market benchmarks, and internal equity across similar roles. The salary range of this position is$84,170-$97,000 New hires typically start toward the lower end of the range, depending on experience and alignment with the role’s scope. In addition to base salary, this position includes an annual bonus target of 5% and eligibility for merit-based increases, which are tied to both individual and organizational performance.

Benefits   

We offer an array of benefits including:

  • Medical, dental, vision insurance
  • 403b retirement match with immediate vesting
  • Group life, AD&D, and short- and long-term disability
  • Optional voluntary life, AD&D and accident plans
  • Health savings or flexible spending accounts

  • Comprehensive leaves of absence (including generous parental leave)

  • Potential for bonuses and merit increases
  • Discount marketplace (gym memberships, pet insurance, etc.)
  • Hybrid / remote work options
  • Team retreats and geographic meetups
  • Rewards and recognition programs

Diversity     

We know that the diversity of our teams makes us stronger as an organization, and RMI is dedicated to the principles of equal employment opportunity as outlined in U.S. federal law. We prohibit discrimination against applicants, interns, and employees on the basis of any legally recognized basis, including but not limited to: age (40 and over), race, color, sex, pregnancy (including lactation, childbirth, or related medical conditions), religion, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing and characteristics), sexual orientation, gender expression/identity, uniformed service member status, veteran status, citizenship status, or any other applicable status protected by applicable law.

Every therapist on the remote caseload starts with six in-person brace fittings on patients from your own current caseload, so you know the devices you will be coaching patients on. This is not a sales role. We do not ask you to refer; you treat patients you already see.

Teletherapy patient referrals from PeteDME begin: our patients, work from home, on your schedule, paid per visit and per call.

• Free specialized training and certification in orthopedic bracing.

• Keep your current job. This is additional, independent-contractor work alongside it.
• Flat fees fixed in advance; no part of your pay depends on volume or on referrals.

Requirements

    • Active physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license in the state where you practice.
    • Currently working in home health or another in-home setting.
    • You evaluate and provide treatment.

How to apply

This leader will work closely with team members of the Data Lakehouse Engineering teams.


The vision behind Wex’s AI/ML engineering is to create a unified, scalable, and intelligent data and compute infrastructure that empowers our organization to unlock the full potential of our data.


We are looking for a highly motivated, technically deep, and experienced Software Engineer to join the org and design, architect the AI/ML engineering applications and frameworks for Wex.

This role can also be in Chicago, Portland, Maine (Wex HQ), or Boston. The ideal candidate will be a hands-on leader with deep technical expertise in building and scaling data lake environments, coupled with strong people leadership and communication skills to drive alignment across the organization.


Responsibilities

  • Lead and drive the development of technology and platform for the company's AI/ML engineering needs, ensure the functional richness, reliability, performance, and flexibility of this platform
  • Help design the architecture and lead the implementation of the AI/ML infrastructure, platform and services.
  • Challenge the status quo and hold a high bar to drive for better and better technical solutions to effectively serve all the needs in the broad risk area of Wex.

  • Set a high bar, and provide technical guidance and effective training & mentorship to the engineering teams in your group, including engineering principles, skills, and best practices. Uphold strong DORA metrics across the org. Foster an environment of continuous learning and innovation. Build an inclusive, productive, innovative, and engaging Risk group, including attracting high talents from the industry.
    Guide the leaders in your group to do the same.
  • Set clear, measurable quality goals for your group in a data-driven way
  • Partner with the security org and SRE org to ensure continuous improvement and meeting of security requirements, SLOs, and error budget.
  • Take strong financial responsibility for your team.
  • Hold yourself and your team accountable for delivering quality results using defined OKRs.
  • Advise Senior Leadership team on highly complex situations that impact our organization and then lead teams through the initiative, driving excellent quality results and achieving defined OKRs across the organization.
  • Provide strategic thought leadership on business initiatives using your deep technical and business industry expertise.

Qualifications & Experience

  • A technically deep and innovative Software Engineer leader able to act and deliver to the business needs.
  • Have 15-20 years of software design and development experience at a large scale.
  • Strong software development skills in his or her chosen programming language, but ready and willing to learn and program in Java and Python.
  • Good experience in building machine learning supervised and unsupervised models. Experience in Reinforcement Learning is a plus.
  • Experience in using LLM models a plus
  • Broad understanding of distributed computing frameworks like Ray and Spark
  • Demonstrable experience in Kubernetes and Terraform
  • Experience with Sagemaker a plus
  • Broad understanding of cloud architecture tools and services, such as S3, EMR, Kubernetes, Lambda functions. Experience in AWS and Azure is highly desirable.
  • Deep technically; hands-on in architecture design, development, deployment, and production operation; familiar with agile software development and modern development tools and frameworks; holding strong engineering principles including automation and quality as well as best practices with a high bar. Extensive experience in full software development life cycle E2E including in production monitoring.
  • Rich experience and deep expertise in the areas of Big Data and large scale data platforms, especially in AI and ML.

  • Rich experience in combined engineering practice and agile development. Experienced in leading and guiding teams for effective development using this approach.

Leadership & Personal Characteristics

Beyond experience, the right technical leadership competencies and personal style are critical to success as the Principal AI/ML Engineer. The candidate will model WEX's commitment to innovation, integrity, execution, relationships, community, and the excellence that they commit to their customers. They will have a strong corporate stewardship philosophy and leadership style combined with the following:

Lex Machina fundamentally changes how companies and law firms compete in the business and practice of law. The company provides strategic insights on judges, lawyers, law firms, parties, and other critical information across 20 federal practice areas and a rapidly growing number of state courts. Lex Machina allows law firms and companies to anticipate the behaviors and outcomes that different legal strategies will produce, enabling them to win cases and close business. Based in Silicon Valley, Lex Machina is part of LexisNexis, a leading global provider of legal, regulatory, and business information and analytics. For more information, please visit


About the Role

As a Legal Data Expert - Patent, you will help drive the development of innovative patent litigation and intellectual property analytics products. Working closely with product, engineering, legal, and business teams, you will apply your patent expertise to ensure the accuracy, relevance, and value of patent-focused datasets, analytics, and product features that support legal professionals.

  • Collaborate with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders across Lex Machina and LexisNexis business units to help design, develop, and launch patent-focused analytics that address customer needs and support broader organizational objectives.
  • Translate the questions and workflows of patent litigators, prosecutors, and in-house counsel into product requirements, data definitions, and review rules.

  • Lead a team of attorneys responsible for reviewing patent case data and ensuring the accuracy and completeness of patent analytics.
  • Support customers, marketing initiatives, thought leadership content, webinars, conferences, and industry presentations related to Legal Analytics.
  • Analyze patent litigation trends, significant rulings, and customer feedback to help shape product strategy and innovation.

Requirements

  • Juris Doctor (JD) degree.
  • U.S. patent litigation or prosecution experience as an attorney, patent agent, or USPTO patent examiner; three or more years of relevant patent experience at a law firm, corporate legal department, or the USPTO.
  • Familiarity with IP analytics, patent search, patent prosecution, and related intellectual property workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across business units and cross-functional teams, building strong relationships with technical, legal, and business stakeholders.

HQR

Swimply is the marketplace that lets homeowners rent out their private pools, hot tubs, courts and backyards by the hour. Thousands of hosts across the United States and Canada use Swimply to share space they already own with families and small groups in their community.

We are building a new category of local experiences: places to swim, play, celebrate and spend time together, without owning the space yourself. Our next stage of growth depends on making Swimply part of how people plan their free time and helping more homeowners see the earning potential in their backyards.

You will lead that effort, working directly with our CEO, Product, Operations and Finance teams.

The Role

The Head of Marketing owns how people discover Swimply, make their first booking and come back. You will lead marketing strategy, budget, team and execution across guest acquisition, host acquisition, retention and brand.

Two areas are central to this role: building creator, influencer and ambassador programs that grow an engaged community, and running impactful experiential marketing campaigns that bring the joy of Swimply to life. We are looking for extensive, hands-on experience in both.

You should know how to recruit the right creators, build lasting ambassador relationships and turn an event or activation into something people want to attend, share and book. You will combine that creative judgment with the financial discipline to measure results and expand the programs that work.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will set the strategy, manage the team and partners, and stay close to the work from concept through execution.

What You Will Do

Build creator, influencer and ambassador programs

  • Own the creator and influencer strategy, from identifying partners and negotiating agreements to briefing content, managing relationships and measuring results.
  • Build an ambassador program that gives creators, hosts and guests a meaningful way to introduce their communities to Swimply.
  • Develop ongoing relationships with partners who can authentically show the experiences available on the platform.
  • Create clear incentives, expectations and support so ambassadors stay engaged and produce results.
  • Turn successful collaborations into repeatable programs that drive awareness, first bookings and repeat usage.
  • Work with creators and the internal team to develop compelling content for organic social, paid campaigns and other marketing channels.

Bring Swimply to life through experiences

Grow the community and brand

  • Develop partnerships with brands, local businesses and community organizations that introduce Swimply to relevant audiences.
  • Maintain a steady pipeline of creative concepts and customer stories that show people what they can do on Swimply.

Own marketing strategy and results

  • Build the marketing plan around bookings, revenue, new customers and repeat usage, with clear targets by channel and market.

  • Own the marketing budget and work with Finance to evaluate acquisition costs, payback and contribution after marketing spend.

Part-Time Instructor – Cybersecurity

About Us

Simplilearn is the world’s #1 online Bootcamp provider, enabling learners around the globe with rigorous and highly specialised training offered in partnership with world-renowned universities and leading corporations. We focus on emerging technologies and skills, such as data science, cloud computing, programming, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, product management, and more—skills that are transforming the global economy. Our training is hands-on and immersive, including live virtual classes, integrated labs and projects, 24x7 support, and a collaborative learning environment. Over two million professionals and 2,000 corporate training organisations across 150 countries have harnessed our award-winning programmes to achieve their career and business goals.

Simplilearn has collaborated with Fullstack Academy to leverage its widespread footprint in the US region and partnerships with top US universities to grow internationally.

Position Overview

The Part-Time Instructor – Cybersecurity plays a key role in delivering engaging, practical, and impactful learning experiences to adult learners enrolled in Simplilearn's online Cybersecurity programmes.

The instructor will facilitate live online training sessions covering core cybersecurity principles, information security, network security, threat detection, vulnerability management, security operations, incident response, risk management, and industry-standard security practices.

This role requires a combination of strong technical expertise, practical industry experience, and instructional capabilities. The instructor will be responsible for explaining complex cybersecurity concepts, demonstrating security tools and techniques, facilitating hands-on exercises, and connecting theoretical knowledge with real-world cybersecurity scenarios.

The ideal candidate will have professional experience in cybersecurity, information security, network security, security operations, penetration testing, or related domains, along with the ability to guide learners through practical security challenges and industry use cases.

Classes are delivered 100% online in a synchronous, instructor-led format.

Key Responsibilities

Instruction & Student Engagement

  • Deliver assigned lessons aligned with curriculum learning objectives, instructional materials, and session plans.
  • Facilitate engaging live online training sessions using effective instructional practices for adult learners.
  • Provide subject matter expertise across Cybersecurity and Information Security domains.
  • Explain cybersecurity concepts, frameworks, tools, and industry best practices through practical examples and demonstrations.
  • Connect course content to real-world industry applications, security challenges, and professional practices.
  • Facilitate hands-on labs, technical exercises, group activities, and scenario-based learning.
  • Encourage collaboration, critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and problem-solving within the classroom.
  • Demonstrate practical approaches to identifying, analysing, preventing, and responding to cybersecurity threats.
  • Support learners in developing the technical skills required for cybersecurity roles.

Cybersecurity Knowledge Areas

The instructor should be comfortable teaching and discussing relevant topics across areas such as:

  • Cybersecurity fundamentals and information security principles.
  • Network security and network architecture.
  • Operating system security, including Windows and Linux.
  • Security protocols, encryption, and cryptography fundamentals.
  • Identity and Access Management (IAM).
  • Authentication, authorisation, and access control.
  • Vulnerability assessment and management.
  • Threat intelligence and threat analysis.
  • Security monitoring and Security Operations Centre (SOC) fundamentals.
  • Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).
  • Incident detection, response, and recovery.
  • Penetration testing and ethical hacking fundamentals.
  • Application and web security.
  • Cloud security fundamentals.
  • Endpoint security and endpoint protection.
  • Malware analysis and prevention.
  • Risk assessment and security governance.
  • Security policies, compliance, and regulatory frameworks.
  • Security awareness and human-centric security practices.
  • Business continuity and disaster recovery.
  • Emerging cybersecurity threats, attack techniques, and defence strategies.

Student Support & Mentorship

  • Provide individualised student support during live sessions and scheduled office hours.
  • Maintain regular communication with students regarding progress, expectations, learning milestones, and skill development.
  • Respond to student and staff communications in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide clear, constructive, and timely feedback on assignments, practical exercises, and assessments.
  • Mentor students in developing practical cybersecurity skills and industry-relevant knowledge.
  • Help learners understand real-world security challenges and apply appropriate security practices.
  • Identify learning difficulties and provide additional guidance where necessary.

Performance Monitoring

  • Evaluate student progress based on course deliverables, practical exercises, assessments, and established grading rubrics.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of student performance, attendance, and engagement.
  • Identify and escalate academic or performance concerns to the Learner Experience Manager or appropriate staff.
  • Support performance improvement plans when necessary.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives to enhance instructional quality and student outcomes.

Collaboration & Professional Conduct

  • Adhere to institutional policies, curriculum requirements, and instructional team standards.
  • Foster an inclusive, respectful, collaborative, and professional learning environment.
  • Serve as a role model and mentor for students entering or advancing within the cybersecurity industry.
  • Collaborate with instructional staff and programme teams to improve the student learning experience.
  • Share relevant industry insights, practical examples, and emerging cybersecurity trends.
  • Represent Simplilearn Academy professionally when interacting with students, staff, and external stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

Applicants must meet one of the following criteria:

  • Bachelor's degree in any field AND a minimum of 3 years of professional experience in Cybersecurity.

OR

  • A minimum of 5 years of professional experience in Cybersecurity without a bachelor's degree.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong professional knowledge and practical expertise in Cybersecurity and Information Security.
  • Demonstrated experience working in one or more cybersecurity domains, including network security, security operations, threat detection, vulnerability management, penetration testing, incident response, or cloud security.
  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, security frameworks, industry standards, and best practices.
  • Familiarity with commonly used cybersecurity tools, platforms, and technologies.
  • Ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to learners with different levels of technical knowledge.
  • Ability to connect theoretical cybersecurity concepts with practical industry applications.
  • Passion for education, mentoring, and developing future cybersecurity professionals.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to facilitate engaging and interactive online learning experiences.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fully remote teaching environment.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience delivering technical training, workshops, or instructor-led sessions in Cybersecurity.
  • Experience mentoring junior cybersecurity professionals or individuals transitioning into cybersecurity careers.
  • Relevant industry certifications such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, CEH, CISM, CISA, CCSP, CySA+, or equivalent certifications.
  • Hands-on experience with security tools such as Wireshark, Nmap, Metasploit, Burp Suite, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or similar platforms.
  • Experience working with SIEM solutions, vulnerability assessment tools, endpoint protection platforms, and security monitoring technologies.
  • Experience with penetration testing, ethical hacking, incident response, or security operations.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, MITRE ATT&CK, and CIS Controls.
  • Exposure to cloud security platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Experience creating practical cybersecurity exercises, labs, assignments, or technical demonstrations.
  • Strong understanding of current cybersecurity threats, attack vectors, and defensive security practices.

Key Competencies

  • Strong cybersecurity subject matter expertise.
  • Excellent instructional and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to simplify complex cybersecurity concepts through practical examples.
  • Strong analytical thinking and technical problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills.
  • Ability to engage and mentor adult learners.
  • Strong professional presence in a virtual classroom environment.
  • Ability to encourage collaborative and hands-on learning.
  • Passion for cybersecurity education and professional development.
  • Commitment to maintaining current knowledge of cybersecurity technologies and industry trends.

Work Schedule

Part-Time instructors typically work 10–13 hours per week, depending on cohort schedules.

Current Cybersecurity cohorts are scheduled to meet during evening hours:

  • Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday
  • Sessions typically run 6:30 PM – 9:30 PM CST.

Flexibility for evening availability is required.

Compensation

The anticipated pay range for this position is $50 per hour.

Candidates with strong cybersecurity industry experience, relevant professional certifications, hands-on technical expertise, and instructional capabilities are encouraged to apply.

This position is classified as Part-Time, Non-Exempt, and employees will be compensated for all hours worked in accordance with applicable federal and state wage and hour laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout employment.

Netrio is a leading managed services provider delivering IT and cybersecurity solutions to small and mid-market organizations across North America. Netrio is seeking a Cybersecurity Consultant to support cybersecurity consulting, assessment, governance, risk, and compliance engagements for our clients.

This client-facing role requires a combination of cybersecurity knowledge, analytical ability, strong written and verbal communication, and excellent organizational skills. The Cybersecurity Consultant will work with other consultants, project managers, technical teams, and client stakeholders to assess cybersecurity environments, document findings, develop recommendations, and support the delivery of cybersecurity projects and ongoing client programs.

The ideal candidate can take ownership of work, manage multiple priorities, move projects forward independently, identify when assistance or escalation is needed, and clearly communicate project status to internal and client stakeholders.

What you'll do

  • Perform cybersecurity assessments against recognized security frameworks, standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

  • Take ownership of assigned projects and activities from initiation through completion, including tracking tasks, dependencies, outstanding information, deliverables, and deadlines.
  • Maintain awareness of project status and proactively communicate progress, risks, delays, dependencies, and required decisions to project managers and other stakeholders.

  • Work independently

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 2 to 4 years of relevant cybersecurity, risk, or GRC experience, ideally in a consulting, MSP, or advisory setting.

  • Experience performing security or compliance assessments, including reviewing policies, interviewing stakeholders, and evaluating technical evidence.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, professional reports and recommendations for technical and executive audiences.
  • Strong verbal communication skills and a client-facing presence, including the ability to explain risk in business terms.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines, work independently, and proactively communicate project status.

  • Experience in an MSP or professional services environment, particularly with small and mid-market clients.

How This Position Impacts Others
