jobs.excerpt: About UsAt Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care.
jobs.description:
About Us

At Prenuvo, we are on a mission to flip the paradigm from reactive “sick-care” to proactive health care. Our award-winning whole body scan is fast (under 1 hour), safe (MRI has no ionizing radiation), and non-invasive (no contrast). Our unique integrated stack of optimized hardware, software, and increasingly AI, coupled with the patient-centric experience across our domestic and global clinics, have allowed us to lead the change against “we caught it too late again".

The Commercial Implementation Lead is the connective tissue between Sales and the rest of the business for B2B contracts across Physician, Enterprise, and Strategic Partnerships. This role owns cross-functional alignment on what Prenuvo commits to in a contract and when we can deliver it — partnering with sales leaders to pressure-test any obligations that require Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales Ops, Marketing, and Legal before signature, then converting signed terms into a sequenced launch plan and driving it to go-live and beyond.

This is an operational partnership role. The Commercial Implementation Lead works shoulder-to-shoulder with sales leadership, and Account Managers as their operational counterpart: the person who tells them what is deliverable, on what timeline, at what cost, and who then makes it happen. This role does not source or close new business; it exists to make sure what we sign is achievable, implemented well, stays compliant, and performs.

This role does not provide visa sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada at the time of hire and must not require employer sponsorship for a work visa (current or future).

Help reshape the world through proactive healthcare while working with cutting-edge technology and high performing teams with deep expertise - join us to make a difference in people’s lives!

What You'll Do

Cross-Functional Alignment on Commitments

  • Serve as the single point of accountability for cross-functional alignment on contractual commitments — what Prenuvo agrees to deliver, by when, and at what operational cost — across Physician, Enterprise, and Strategic Partnerships.
  • Partner with Sales during deal construction to pressure-test new proposed terms against operational reality, convening Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales Ops, Legal, and Marketing to confirm feasibility, sequencing, and delivery timelines before commitments are made.
  • Translate business asks from Sales into clear requirements for internal teams, and translate internal constraints back into terms Sales can negotiate with confidence.
  • Escalate and resolve conflicts between what a deal requires and what the business can support, driving to a documented decision rather than an open question.
  • Maintain a shared record of standard versus non-standard commitments, so repeat asks are answered consistently and quickly and one-off exceptions are visible and deliberate.

Implementation and Launch Execution

  • Own post-sale implementation for all executed contracts from signature through go-live, receiving handoff from Sales and channel leaders and converting contract terms into an operational launch plan with named owners and dates.
  • Lead launches across all three channels, coordinating Marketing, Sales Ops, Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and external stakeholders against a shared timeline.
  • Partner with Finance and Sales Ops on the operational mechanics of each contract — billing and invoicing setup, pricing and discount structures, revenue recognition inputs, quota and crediting implications, and reporting requirements.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering where contracts require configuration, integration, data exchange, or roadmap-dependent deliverables; hold the line on what is committed versus what is aspirational.
  • Ensure compliance with all contractual, marketing, clinical, and operational deliverables across each channel, and track obligations through their full lifecycle.

Operational Partnership to Sales

  • Act as the operational partner to sales leaders and Account Managers, providing visibility into implementation status, delivery risk, and what can realistically be promised to accounts in flight.
  • Participate in pipeline and account reviews to flag downstream operational implications early and keep commercial and delivery expectations aligned.
  • Equip Account Managers with the operational detail they need for renewal, expansion, and escalation conversations.

Systems, Data, and Performance

  • Develop and manage centralized tracking of contacts in Salesforce, contract terms, engagement metrics, content performance, and preferences across Physician, Enterprise, and Strategic Partnerships.
  • Monitor implementation and post-launch performance metrics by channel, and translate insights into actions that drive account and partnership growth.
  • Build the reporting and dashboards that give Sales, Finance, and leadership a shared view of commitments outstanding, launches in flight, and delivery risk.

Relationship Management and Retention

  • Uphold strong company representation and retain relationships with external partners post-launch to drive continued growth and long-term success (where applicable).
  • Track account and partner satisfaction, proactively surfacing and addressing risks to ensure long-term retention across all channels.
  • Develop and sustain strong relationships through consistent, high-touch engagement and professionalism, tailored to the distinct dynamics of Physician, Enterprise, and Strategic Partnership relationships.
  • Maintain confidentiality and HIPAA compliance when interacting with physicians, enterprise clients, and partners.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5–8 years in implementation, onboarding, deal desk, contract operations, revenue operations, or partner/account management, ideally spanning more than one type of commercial relationship (transactional and partnership-based).
  • Demonstrated track record of driving cross-functional alignment without direct authority — bringing Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales Ops, Legal, and Marketing to a shared decision on scope and timing, and holding them to it.
  • Experience acting as the operational counterpart to a sales organization, partnering directly with sales leaders and Account Managers on what can be committed and delivered.
  • Hands-on Salesforce experience is required, including building and maintaining reports, dashboards, and custom tracking structures; experience partnering with Sales Ops on CRM design and data integrity strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to read and operationalize contract terms accurately without formal legal training.
  • Working fluency with the commercial mechanics of a deal — pricing and discounting, billing and invoicing, revenue recognition implications — sufficient to partner credibly with Finance.
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent launches with competing timelines and varying complexity across different stakeholder types.
  • Comfort translating between commercial and technical audiences, including scoping product or engineering dependencies with enough precision to set a realistic delivery date.
  • Healthcare, diagnostics, or other regulated-industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Ability to shift tone and approach across distinct relationship types: clinical/physician, enterprise procurement, and strategic partne

Our Values

First: we are Pioneers

  • Transforming healthcare requires divergent thinking, bias for action, disciplined experimentation, and consistent grit and determination to maintain momentum. This journey is as challenging as it is rewarding.

Second: we are Platform-Builders

  • We’re always building foundations that allow us to achieve tomorrow more than we did today. We never lose sight of what’s ahead – in a mindset of ownership and duty to our mission.

Above all: we are Patients

  • We could all be the next person who walks through our very doors, seeking clarity or peace of mind. We are proud of our impact on our patients’ lives, and we won’t stop till everyone can benefit from our work.

What We Offer

  • An avenue to make a positive impact on people's lives and their health
  • We believe in preventive healthcare for everyone. This role includes whole-body scans as part of our employee benefits
  • Growth opportunities are at the heart of our people journey, we’re doing big things with bright minds - there is no single path to success, it can be shaped along the way
  • Building strong relationships is at the core of everything we do - our team gets together each week to connect, share, and socialize
  • Recognizing time away to restore is vital to our wellbeing - we have a flexible vacation policy and we will encourage you to use it
  • We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, including Mental Health coverage, to support you and your family
  • Prenuvo offers eligible Canadian employees access to both RRSP and TFSA retirement savings plans, with immediate, optional enrollment and the flexibility to invest and save for the future on your own terms. While Prenuvo provides access to these plans, the company does not currently offer matching contributions.
  • The base salary for this role ranges from $96,000-$113,000 in local currency, depending upon experience and geographic location

We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

As part of the hiring process, successful candidates will undergo a background check in compliance to applicable federal, provincial, and state rules.

If you are contacted by a recruiter, please ensure their email address ends with @prenuvo.com. We do not use third-party recruitment services or any other email domains for hiring purposes. This is a hands-on outbound sales role focused on cold calling, email outreach, LinkedIn prospecting, lead qualification, follow-up, and meeting generation.

You’ll research prospective companies and decision-makers, start conversations with potential customers, communicate the company’s value proposition, qualify interest, handle objections, and book qualified meetings for the sales team.

If you’re comfortable with outbound outreach, motivated by targets, and enjoy turning cold prospects into sales conversations, this role is a strong fit.

Outbound Prospecting & Lead Generation

jobs.excerpt: BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals.
jobs.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:

The Senior Manager, Digital Clinical Operations is responsible to enhance Global Clinical Operations productivity and reduce clinical trial inefficiencies, by setting the strategy, as well as shaping, defining, and delivering business critical digital capabilities. This role will provide digital leadership across investigator fee management, study and site budgeting, site contracting, payment and invoice management, reconciliation, forecasting and variance analytics. The Senior Manager will lead cross-functional digital initiatives from opportunity identification and business case development through implementation, adoption, and value realization, partnering across GCO, technical and data teams, and external technology providers.

The technology ecosystem includes a combination of anchor applications, both homegrown and SaaS, exploratory innovations, as well as analytics capabilities.

This role will specifically focus on following activities:

· Define and detail enhancements for digital solutions used by the budgeting, site contracting, payment and data hub teams.

· Engage with clinical stakeholders across geographies and functions, to create a clear voice of the clinical teams for the purpose of the delivery of enhancements.

· Lead the execution and delivery of digital solution pilots and explorations by defining scope, objectives, deliverables, timelines, milestones, and success criteria; mobilizing cross-functional teams; coordinating vendor onboarding; monitoring dependencies, actions, risks, issues, and costs; providing transparent status reporting; and escalating decisions or barriers to ensure timely, high-quality delivery

· Lead the translation of business strategy, operational needs, and stakeholder requirements into digital capability requirements and roadmaps, ensuring organizational, regional, and process alignment.

· Facilitate the prioritization of demand, managing competing interests with objective assessment of value. Ensure that priorities are aligned to organizational priorities. Create transparency into priorities with clear communication to stakeholders. Translate priorities into plans in collaboration with the development team. Manage expectations with stakeholders.

· Provide business leadership for the development of business requirements, as well as hands-on authoring, ensuring requirements appropriately address business outcomes, process needs, compliance considerations, data requirements, and intended value.

· Participate with the implementation team in sprint planning, sprint testing, and SDLC testing.

· Oversee and direct UAT and business testing, partnering with the business lead on the testing strategy and approach, establishing a UAT plan, mobilizing the UAT team, overseeing scripting, and coordinating UAT activities within the framework of the implementation plan.

· Ensure that all digital capabilities have a defined business process, partnering with the GCO business lead.

· As part of requirement gathering, ensure that related business processes are well defined and probe into process optimization or process solutions where appropriate, to complement digital solutioning. In cases where process or process ownership is not defined, create process flows aligned with proper functions and leadership.

· Define and articulate the value proposition of all requests, in both quantifiable and qualitative categories.

· Define, track and share business outcome value measures for digital projects.

· Represent GCO business interests as a key member of the implementation team.

· Review proposed designs to ensure that solutions are architected to meet the actual need and expected value. Ensure data are fit for intended decision-making.

· Drive business demand prioritization within assigned capability areas, balancing business value, risk, strategic alignment, dependencies, and resource constraints in partnership with product and technology teams. Own curation of backlog.

· Partner with business lead to ensure appropriate change management and business adoption plans are in place.

· Evaluate emerging technologies, industry solutions, and vendor capabilities and provide recommendations to GCO leadership regarding adoption, investment, experimentation, and scale-up.

The incumbent will work directly with GCO clinical stakeholders, Development and IT organizations and support implementing novel technology solutions.

Essential Functions of the job:

General expectations of a Digital Clinical Operations employee

  • Forge relationships with users to understand their requirements and processes, identify automation opportunities, collaborate with development/vendor team to create the necessary fit-for-purpose solutions.
  • Project Management: ensure forward progress, timelines are managed, accountabilities are clear, and project risks and costs are managed.
  • Drive the analysis of the technology and industry trends to identify specific opportunities that ensure BeOne clinical trials and operations are conducted with fit-for-purpose, cost-effective and innovative solutions that are cohesive, efficient, reliable, and compliant with all applicable regulatory expectations.
  • Implement the GCO technology roadmap to increase Global Clinical Operations’ productivity, reduce rising costs of clinical trials, and reduce clinical trial inefficiencies
  • Monitor, evaluate, and optimize the performance and quality of the technology solutions, as well as troubleshoot and resolve any issues that may arise
  • Promote a culture that exemplifies agility, compliance, process-orientation, data-driven decision-making, and thoughtful use of technology and innovation
  • Partner with internal BeOne departments, including Development Data Science, QA and IT, to support the development of documentation associated with computerized systems, including lifecycle management for existing systems, and the implementation of innovative new systems
  • Develop solution requirements and standards in alignment with stakeholders (Clinical Operations, Data Management, Supply Chain, etc.).
  • Identify pain points and manual workflows, and develop technological solutions that address these challenges, leveraging existing and innovative approaches.
  • Take accountability for business value realization of technology solutions. Ensure that appropriate change tactics are planned and effectively delivered (communications, training, user communities, adoption drives) for both internal and external users. May directly involve development and delivery of these tactics.
  • Focus on user expectation and satisfaction and decreasing user burden. Proactively ensure system usability and user needs remain a high priority.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Be an individual contributor
  • Provide functional leadership to analysts, consultants, vendors, and matrixed project resources supporting assigned digital initiatives. Provide coaching, direction, and subject-matter guidance while establishing clear accountability for deliverables and outcomes.

Technical Skills:

  • Requirement gathering and documentation
  • Technical solution project management
  • Process modeling
  • Familiarity with clinical operations applications in the financial space

Soft skills:

  • Stakeholder management: Ability to work collaboratively with functional leadership and external partners, to forge partnerships and collaborations arrangements. Ability to manage expectations, to communicate to broad groups of end-users.
  • Project management leadership: Ability to build alignment, influence without direct authority, foster accountability, navigate competing priorities, adapt to change, and maintain constructive collaboration and forward momentum across cross-functional teams.
  • Communication: Exhibits strong cross-cultural awareness, and strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively convey complex insights to non-technical stakeholders
  • Cross-functional oversight: Ability to collaborate with cross-functional clinical teams to understand their business needs and deliver outcome-aligned solutions. Partner with internal BeiGene departments, including Development Data Science, QA and IT, to develop standards, policies, and procedures associated with computerized systems, including lifecycle management for existing systems, and the implementation of innovative new systems.
  • Problem-Solving: Excellent conceptual, analytical, and problem-solving skills to identify trends and make data-driven decisions. Troubleshooting skills.

· Able to drive forward progress

· Comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, and able to adapt to changes in responsibilities and workloads

Required experience:

  • Clinical Operations domain experience – working in Biotech, life sciences or IT consulting industry
  • Bachelor’s degree Computer Science, Life Sciences, Business or related degree required
  • Minimum 7+ years in translating business needs into technology solutions with a proven record
  • Minimum 2 years in driving execution and delivery of solutions
  • Investigator fee management systems (CMS, ERP, budgeting systems, payment systems, financial analytics, forecasting, accruals)
  • Budgeting, contracting, payment expertise in the context of clinical trials
  • Core clinical systems (CTMS, eDC, IRT)
  • SDLC
  • Validated systems
  • Project management experience is a plus
  • Business analysis experience is a plus
  • Familiarity with data processing / engineering is a plus

Travel: As needed

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

  • Fosters Teamwork
  • Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
  • Self-Awareness
  • Acts Inclusively
  • Demonstrates Initiative
  • Entrepreneurial Mindset
  • Continuous Learning
  • Embraces Change
  • Results-Oriented
  • Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
  • Financial Excellence
  • Communicates with Clarity

jobs.excerpt: Columbia Human Rights Graduate Fellowship: Corporate Legal Accountability Fellow This opportunity is only open to those enrolled on the Columbia Human Rights Graduate Fellowship Program.
jobs.description:
Columbia Human Rights Graduate Fellowship: Corporate Legal Accountability Fellow

This opportunity is only open to those enrolled on the Columbia Human Rights Graduate Fellowship Program. External applicants will not be considered.

About the opportunity

The Business and Human Rights Centre (BHRC) team is seeking an enthusiastic, reliable lawyer committed to human rights to join its Corporate Legal Accountability (CLA) Programme for one year. This fellowship offers a unique opportunity to support communities, advocates and lawyers seeking access to remedy, contribute to cutting-edge research and advocacy on corporate accountability, and help expand the only global information hub on corporate legal accountability.

Through the CLA Programme, BHRC tracks strategic lawsuits against companies over alleged human rights abuses and monitors legislative developments that can help strengthen corporate accountability. The fellow will carry out research, develop advocacy tools, and contribute to influencing strategies aligned with BHRC’s strategic plan, helping lawyers and legal advocates enhance communities’ access to legal remedy.

What you will work on

  • Just energy transition litigation: The fellow will support the development of BHRC’s flagship emerging just energy transition litigation portfolio, a subset of climate change litigation in which Indigenous Peoples, frontline communities, or affected workers bring rights-based lawsuits concerning the “distribution of benefits and burdens” of the transition away from fossil fuels and towards net-zero emissions. This may include contributing to the strategic vision of the project, researching new cases for the Just Transition Litigation Tracking Tool, supporting the related yearly analysis, and liaising with partners.
  • UN legally binding instrument: The fellow will support BHRC’s advocacy on the UN legally binding instrument to regulate transnational corporations and other companies with respect to human rights. This may include helping to organise webinars, liaising with experts and partners for the “Debate the treaty” blog series, monitoring the UN Intergovernmental Working Group session, and contributing to Daily Updates summarising key takeaways of the session.
  • Strategic litigation database: The fellow will research legal information, draft or update lawsuit profiles for BHRC’s database of 300+ global cases brought against companies over alleged human rights abuses. This work supports lawyers, legal practitioners and affected people by tracking and analysing litigation trends that can strengthen cases and improve access to legal remedy.
  • Strategic Litigation Network: The fellow will support the development of a Strategic Litigation Network in Africa, building on BHRC’s network in Latin America. The network brings together lawyers, NGOs, human rights defenders and other experts to share strategies, tools and good practices for corporate accountability.
  • Regular programme outputs: The fellow will draft and develop CLA Programme publications, including the Quarterly Update, BHRC’s newsletter highlighting timely topics and key developments in corporate legal accountability.

Learning opportunities and professional development

As a fellow, you will gain practical experience in an international NGO and become an integral member of a diverse and international team. You will strengthen your legal research and analytical skills while supporting lawyers and communities seeking greater accountability for business-related human rights abuses. You will also learn from colleagues across the world, deepen your knowledge of the business and human rights field, and have opportunities to liaise with civil society, lawyers and other key stakeholders working on corporate legal accountability globally.

Throughout the fellowship, you will have the opportunity to publish research on BHRC’s website, access BHRC’s data, and gain experience using internet-based publication tools such as Mailchimp and the Wagtail content management system.

Working environment

BHRC offers a fully remote working environment, with regular contact via Microsoft Teams. As a global organisation, BHRC works with colleagues around the world on a daily basis, creating a truly international workplace. If you are already based in London or Berlin and have the right to work in the UK or Germany, there may be opportunities to work from one of BHRC’s offices.

Your will work closely with your direct supervisor based in France, and with the Director of International Programmes based in South Africa as well as colleagues across BHRC's global network.

Eligibility criteria

  • Currently enrolled in, or recently completed (class of 2025 or 2026, depending on the fellowship), a postgraduate legal degree (LLM/JD or similar) from Columbia Law School.
  • Secure funding from the Columbia Fellowship Program.
  • Demonstrated academic or professional experience carrying out international and/or multi-jurisdictional legal research, analysis and summarising information.
  • Interest in and commitment to promoting human rights, especially business and human rights.
  • Excellent English language skills, including reading, writing and speaking. Fluency in another language, such as French, Spanish, Arabic or Russian, is a plus.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently and exercise sound judgement in a remote working environment.

Application timeline

Application deadline: 29 November 2026, close of business EST. Interviews are planned for late November/early December.

About BHRC

The Business and Human Rights Centre (BHRC) is a global non-profit organisation that works with communities, civil society, companies and governments to put human rights at the heart of business, deliver a just economy, climate justice, and end abuse. BHRC tracks the human rights policies and practices of more than 10,000 companies worldwide to push for stronger human rights protections. Its website is a global business and human rights knowledge hub, delivering daily news in 11 languages to more than 150,000 active users per month. BHRC’s weekly e-newsletter has over 16,000 subscribers globally, including advocates, business people, governments, investors and the UN.

BHRC’s Corporate Legal Accountability (CLA) Programme aims to strengthen the legal accountability of business actors so that rightsholders can exercise their rights and access justice when abuses occur. We view strategic litigation as a critical tool for challenging impunity. Through networks, analysis and information, we equip lawyers, legal practitioners and affected people around the world to build stronger cases against companies implicated in human rights abuses, support novel legal strategies, establish effective legal precedent and improve access to legal remedy.

In practice, the CLA Programme contributes to BHRC’s strategic goals of shared prosperity for society, corporate duty of care for human rights and environmental justice, and a safe and enabling environment for communities and workers through the following activities:

  • Advancing corporate accountability through legal analysis and strategic insights: we analyse timely topics and share key legal developments through our CLA Quarterly Update, providing concise and accessible information on corporate legal accountability legislative developments and landmark lawsuits for grassroots and community practitioners.
  • Monitoring legal and legislative developments related to business and human rights, including the UN Binding Treaty. Given BHRC’s current thematic priorities, the CLA Programme tracks legal news linked to natural resources and the just energy transition, tech and human rights, and labour rights.
  • Strengthening strategic litigation against corporate abuse: we maintain and expand our lawsuit profiles database, which documents 300+ cases brought against companies over allegations of human rights abuses. The database is one of the world's most comprehensive freely accessible repository of corporate legal accountability cases and judgments, providing legal advocates with insight into trends, challenges and emerging jurisprudence on strategic litigation for corporate accountability.
  • Building networks for peer learning and collective action: Through BHRC’s Strategic Litigation Network in Latin America, Legal Assistance Directory and convenings, we foster collaboration and peer-to-peer learning by connecting communities, legal practitioners and other experts from around the world working to address corporate-related harms.

  • Support renewal and expansion conversations with technical proof points: performance data, integration health, and use-case expansion opportunities

In particolare, le attività previste includono:

gestione e riavvio di servizi e processi,

raccolta di log ed evidenze tecniche, gestione degli account e delle credenziali

verifica dei backup e applicazione di patch e mitigazioni.

gestione clienti VIP

controllo di IP, domini e URL, VPN, raccolta dei log

verifica del funzionamento del cluster in alta disponibilità (HA).

gestione degli account e delle sessioni, interventi sulle credenziali e sull'autenticazione MFA

controllo e ripristino dei record DNS.


Requisiti

Competenze tecniche richieste per la posizione:

  • sistemi operativi Windows Server e Linux.
  • Active Directory e gestione di Domain Controller.
  • Azure, in particolare Entra ID e Azure DNS.
  • Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) e delle principali componenti Kubernetes.
  • Microsoft Entra Connect e
  • reti e dei principali protocolli e servizi di rete.
  • firewall, preferibilmente Palo Alto.

Ulteriori competenze e conoscenze

  • Esperienza in attività di Incident Response e supporto alla gestione di incidenti di sicurezza informatica.
  • strumenti EDR e delle procedure di isolamento delle postazioni.
  • raccolta e l'analisi di log, event log e dump di memoria.
  • procedure di backup e restore di server e macchine virtuali.

Seniority professionale richiesta: 2-3 anni di esperienza sulle tecnologie

Modalità di lavoro: da remoto

Tipologia contrattuale proposta: collaborazione in Partita IVA oppure assunzione con CCNL Commercio.

Retribuzione prevista per il ruolo: 190 e/gg (p.iva) oppure 29.000 retribuzione.

The Global HRIS Analyst supports the configuration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of Workday Core HCM. Primary Responsibilities

  • Support colleague lifecycle processes, including Hire, Onboarding, Change Job, Termination, organizational assignments, supervisory organizations, and worker data management.
  • Troubleshoot configuration issues, business process failures, data discrepancies, and system defects; investigate root causes and implement or recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Assess the impact of configuration changes on related Workday modules, business processes, security, reporting, integrations, and downstream systems.
  • Collaborate with teams supporting Recruiting, Compensation, Benefits, Payroll, Absence, Time Tracking, Talent, Learning, Security, and Integrations to coordinate changes and maintain end-to-end process alignment.
  • Support Workday's biannual releases by evaluating new functionality, assessing impacts, configuring approved changes, executing tests, and supporting deployment.
  • Identify opportunities to improve Workday functionality, automate manual processes, reduce recurring issues, and increase operational efficiency.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Workday Core HCM certification or relevant Workday training preferred.

Experience

  • 3-5 years of HRIS experience supporting Workday Core HCM, including hands-on configuration.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into functional solutions and execute Workday configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and implementation.
  • Experience configuring and supporting Workday Core HCM business processes, condition rules, validations, calculated fields, and related configuration components.
  • Experience working across the solution lifecycle, including requirements gathering, impact analysis, solution design, configuration, testing, deployment, and production support.
  • Ability to independently investigate and resolve routine to moderately complex configuration and system issues, recognizing when escalation or additional expertise is needed.

Rémunération

52 500,00 $ à 98 300,00 $ CA par année

Aperçu du poste

L’analyste mondial(e) SIRH (HRIS) soutient la configuration, la maintenance, le dépannage et l’amélioration continue de Workday Core HCM. Responsabilités principales

  • Fournir un soutien fonctionnel et technique pratique pour Workday Core HCM.
  • Recueillir et analyser les besoins d’affaires, documenter les processus opérationnels et convertir ces besoins en solutions fonctionnelles Workday.
  • Configurer et maintenir les fonctionnalités de Workday Core HCM, y compris les processus d’affaires, les règles conditionnelles, les validations, les champs calculés et les composantes de configuration connexes.
  • Réaliser les améliorations assignées tout au long du cycle de vie de la solution, depuis la collecte des exigences et la conception jusqu’à la configuration, les essais, le déploiement, la documentation et la validation postproduction.
  • Soutenir les processus du cycle de vie des employés, notamment l’embauche, l’intégration (onboarding), les changements de poste, les cessations d’emploi, les affectations organisationnelles, les organisations de supervision et la gestion des données des employés.
  • Dépanner les problèmes de configuration, les défaillances des processus d’affaires, les écarts de données et les défauts du système; déterminer les causes fondamentales et mettre en œuvre ou recommander les solutions appropriées.
  • Évaluer les répercussions des changements de configuration sur les modules Workday connexes, les processus d’affaires, la sécurité, les rapports, les intégrations et les systèmes en aval.

  • Soutenir les deux mises à jour annuelles de Workday en évaluant les nouvelles fonctionnalités, en analysant leurs impacts, en configurant les changements approuvés, en exécutant les essais et en soutenant le déploiement.
  • Cerner les occasions d’améliorer les fonctionnalités de Workday, d’automatiser les processus manuels, de réduire les problèmes récurrents et d’accroître l’efficacité opérationnelle.

Formation

  • Certification Workday Core HCM ou formation pertinente sur Workday, un atout.

Expérience

  • Expérience de configuration et de soutien des processus d’affaires de Workday Core HCM, des règles conditionnelles, des validations, des champs calculés et des composantes de configuration connexes.

The Senior Business Process Consultant leads business case development for proposed initiatives, supports the strategic planning process, and leads larger scale, cross-functional initiatives.


Key Details: This position is remote within the United States. Up to 10% travel annually as needed.


  • Leads business case development for proposed initiatives to ensure adequate assessment of opportunities, risks and return on investment.
  • Provides input and supports planning and prioritization of initiatives as part of the strategic and business planning process.
  • Ensures that initiatives support the strategic business plan, meet key business objectives and are executed well tactically.
  • Ensures that all approved business cases are transitioned to initiatives (both documentation and clear responsibilities for each initiative).
  • Leads larger scale, cross-functional initiatives that are intended to drive performance improvement, financial gains, customer satisfaction and improved compliance.
  • Provides strategic and policy guidance on assigned initiatives so that all processes are considered for maximizing effective implementation and results.
  • Organizes work teams, drives consensus and ensures end to end policy/process integrity to accomplish project work: including identification and confirmation of participants, establishment of a project plan, consistent work team engagement and productivity, meeting facilitation, consensus building, recommendation documentation and implementation oversight.
  • Performs detailed analysis of data, workflows, policies, procedures, organization of staff, and skills in order to execute initiatives.
  • Supports the project work by utilizing project management software such as, but not limited to, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, and Microsoft Project.
  • Leads all levels of staff who are responsible for initiatives included in the companies operating plan in order to support their success, development and effective completion and communication of their initiative.
  • Assists other project leaders in specific areas as needed such as facilitation, analysis, process mapping, brain-storming, project management issues, etc.
  • Writes and delivers communication to all levels of organization to ensure support, awareness and effectiveness of process improvement initiatives.
  • Provides other related support as needed to improve the performance of the business
  • Performs other duties as assigned
  • Complies with all policies and standards

Education/Experience:

Bachelor's Degree in a related field or equivalent experience required
Master's Degree in a related field preferred

6+ years managing projects required

Experience in health care and/or insurance preferred

Licenses/Certifications:
Certified Project Management Professional (PMP)-PMI required
Process quality certification preferred

Certified Project Management Professional (PMP)-PMI For Health Net and Enterprise Business Operations only preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Title:

Associate Security Researcher

About Trellix:

Trellix is a global cybersecurity leader helping organizations build cyber resilience for the AI era. Combining AI-native security, operational threat intelligence, and automated detection and response, Trellix provides defense-grade protection at machine speed across on-premises, air-gapped, operational technology, hybrid, and cloud environments. Trellix helps customers anticipate threats, scale effective security operations, maintain business continuity, and adapt their security posture for the modern threat landscape. Working with a broad partner ecosystem and global intelligence collaborators, Trellix helps strengthen the collective defense against cybercriminals and state-sponsored attacks. At Trellix, we empower professionals at all career stages to expand their technical expertise, lead strategic initiatives, and make a tangible global impact. Whether you are an industry pioneer or an emerging specialist, Trellix provides the tools and opportunities to enhance and expand your skill set. Join our mission to scale AI-driven cyber defense alongside an AI-accelerated threat landscape, and help build a safer, more resilient future. More at .

Role Overview:

Join our innovative Security Research team at Trellix, where you'll contribute to the design and development of automated security research and threat detection pipelines, delivering powerful protection capabilities for Trellix endpoint security products. This isn't isolated research work—you'll be building and operating a production-grade automation system that bridges software engineering and threat research, enabling threat analysis, data telemetry, and the seamless generation of security protection policies at machine speed. We're looking for a motivated Associate Security Researcher (or fresh graduate) with a solid foundation in software development and a passion for building robust, scalable, and automated security solutions.

About the Role

  • Design and Develop: Contribute to the design and development of our automated security research and detection pipelines, driving core automation functionality, threat ingestion workflows, and detection tooling from concept through production.
  • End-to-End Ownership: Take ownership of pipeline features and components, from initial design and development through rigorous testing, false-positive validation, automation, and ongoing operational health.
  • Detection Pipeline Development: Build, iterate on, and harden automated threat analysis and detection generation workflows, including automated sample triage, behavioral indicator extraction, and rule deployment across security engines.
  • Deliver Quality: Ensure automated detection rules and pipeline services are delivered on time and to the highest quality standards, meeting research goals and protection commitments.
  • Resilience and Performance: Implement best practices for pipeline resilience, scalability, and performance across high-volume threat telemetry and sample processing systems.
  • Observability and Telemetry: Build and maintain operational instrumentation, logging, and dashboards to monitor pipeline throughput, detection efficacy, and system health.

About You

  • Experience: 0–2+ years of experience (including internships, university research, or strong academic/personal projects; fresh graduates in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, or related fields are strongly encouraged to apply) in Python or backend software development, with a strong interest in security research and automation.
  • Operating Systems: Solid understanding of Linux and/or Windows operating system fundamentals and internals is a must.
  • Security & Detection Knowledge:
    • Foundational understanding of cybersecurity concepts, malware behavior, common vulnerabilities (CVEs, OWASP), and threat analysis.
    • Familiarity with threat detection mechanisms and rule formats (such as YARA, Sigma, Snort, or behavioral signatures).
    • Exposure to static/dynamic malware analysis, sandboxes (e.g., Cuckoo/CAPE), or reverse engineering tools (Ghidra, IDA) through coursework or CTFs.
  • Core Development Skills:
    • Excellent development and debugging skills in Python (or Go / C++).
    • Strong grasp of data structures, algorithms, and software design patterns.
    • CI/CD pipeline experience (Git, GitHub Actions, or equivalent).
    • Strong written communication for technical documentation and async collaboration.
    • Ability to learn quickly and operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.
  • AI/ML & Automation Knowledge:
    • Hands-on experimentation with Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic workflows.
  • Databases & Data Pipelines:
    • SQL / Relational databases such as Postgres or MySQL.
  • Services & Tools:
    • Cloud services familiarity (AWS or GCP).
    • Logging, telemetry, and monitoring tools.
  • Domain Knowledge:
    • Passion for threat intelligence, automated detection engineering, and scaling security research through software.
  • Soft Skills:
    • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across engineering, product, and security research teams.
    • Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to both engineering and research stakeholders.
    • Strong analytical mindset, high coachability, and curiosity for solving complex security challenges through code.

jobs.description:
About Us

Pitchday is a creative agency founded in 2019 in Singapore with a clear vision: to be the go-to creative partner for some of the world’s most desirable brands. We thrive on tackling bold, challenging briefs, and act as a seamless extension of our clients’ teams.

Today, we collaborate with brands across every continent, including Google, YouTube, Android, Netflix, CHANEL, and Silicon Valley startups. Our growth is entirely driven by word of mouth, and our team now spans 10 countries.

Our Team

Our work in Greater China is growing, and we’re looking for a standout Account Director, Greater China to own client relationships in Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. You’ll be the link between our clients there and Pitchday’s global teams in Singapore, Paris, and San Francisco, as well as the design and motion studios we work with across Asia.

You’ll set the standard on the account. That means defining how we work, making briefs clear, removing blockers, and coaching the team until they produce excellent work without needing you in every conversation. You’ll speak with clients in their language and turn their feedback and expectations into direction our creative teams can act on. When a global campaign needs to land in Greater China, you’ll make sure it’s adapted for each market and still on brand.

The Account Directors who do best at Pitchday care deeply about both the client and the creative team. You’ll be the ally of both.

What you will do

  • Own day-to-day delivery for clients in Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, from briefing to final output, so projects launch on time and to the required standard.

  • Be the main point of contact for local clients, in Mandarin (and Cantonese where needed). Give proactive updates and flag risks early.

  • Coordinate between local client teams and Pitchday’s global teams across time zones, so both sides always know what’s agreed, what’s next, and who owns it.

  • Brief and manage design studios, production partners, and freelancers in Greater China and across our regional network, and keep quality, timelines, and budgets under control.

  • Translate Chinese-language briefs and feedback into clear creative direction in English, so designers and producers know exactly what’s needed, why, and by when.

  • Lead the localization of global campaigns for Simplified and Traditional Chinese markets, including copy, cultural review, and market-specific formats.

  • Review concepts and deliverables against brand guidelines, local market expectations, and client requirements before they reach the client.

  • Build and maintain delivery plans, assign ownership, and manage capacity across the account.

  • Track budgets and resourcing, and spot opportunities to grow the account through strong delivery.

  • Mentor designers and account staff and help them grow.

Who you are

  • 7+ years of account or project management in a creative agency, design studio, or production company, working with clients in Greater China.

  • Experience coordinating design studios or external production partners, ideally across several countries.

  • Experience working between global brand teams and local market teams, for example in an international agency’s China office or a global brand’s regional team.

  • Native or fully fluent Mandarin, plus excellent written and spoken English. You’ll write to clients in Chinese and brief the team in English every day.

  • Comfortable working in both Simplified and Traditional Chinese.

  • A strong feel for how brands communicate in Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, and how the three markets differ.

  • Skilled at running creative projects end to end and keeping timelines, budgets, expectations, and scope under control.

  • Detail-oriented, with high standards for creative output and delivery.

  • A supportive leader who can motivate, guide, and grow creative talent.

Nice to have

  • Experience with luxury or tech brands in the region.

  • Working knowledge of local platforms such as WeChat, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Weibo, and Bilibili, and the content formats that work on each.

  • Familiarity with our tools, such as Google Workspace, Slack, Float, and AI platforms like Gemini.

  • A real interest in tech and creativity, and in keeping up with new tools and industry shifts.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary with performance-based bonuses and promotion opportunities.

  • Remote-first setup - work from anywhere.

  • Opportunity to work with flagship clients, including Google, Netflix, and Chanel.

  • Flexible, industry-leading PTO so you can balance work and life your way.

  • Join a talented, inspiring, and collaborative team.

We’re committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels comfortable, regardless of your identity, experiences and beliefs. We want Pitchday to be a place where you can try out new things with the risk of failing, where you can take ownership over your own work without being micromanaged, and where there’s a low barrier for coming up with ideas — no matter your job title or discipline.

How to Apply

  • Click Apply. Share your CV and portfolio link with us.

  • Relevant candidates would be called out for a short screening call.

jobs.title: Managing Project Director
jobs.excerpt: EDC works with federal, state, and community partners to strengthen maternal and child health systems and the workforce supporting families from pregnancy through childhood and adolescence.
jobs.description:
EDC works with federal, state, and community partners to strengthen maternal and child health systems and the workforce supporting families from pregnancy through childhood and adolescence. This work includes, but is not limited to, home visiting, midwifery, doula support, care coordination, and workforce development and technical assistance.

The Managing Project Director provides strategic and operational leadership to advance EDC’s maternal and child health (MCH) work. As a strategic partner to the Director of Maternal and Child Health, this role helps lead the growth and diversification of EDC’s MCH portfolio. To do this successfully, the role cultivates relationships across federal, state, philanthropic, and other sectors, identifies and shapes new funding opportunities, and expands MCH work in alignment with EDC’s strengths and emerging public health priorities. Additionally, the Managing Project Director provides senior oversight of complex, large-scale projects and initiatives and in collaboration with other project leaders, connects project-level work to the goals of the MCH area of focus and EDC’s broader strategy.

Reporting to the Director of Maternal and Child Health, the Managing Project Director brings deep public health experience, an established external network, and expertise in areas such as policy or financing in order to steward fundable initiatives and strategic partnerships, cultivate philanthropic opportunities, and strengthen EDC’s national visibility, credibility, and thought leadership in MCH.

This role may be located in one of EDC's offices or remote within the United States.

You Will:

  • Partner with the Director of Maternal and Child Health on the development and execution of plans to advance EDC’s MCH work as an area of focus within EDC’s Be Well strategy area, identifying and pursuing opportunities that support sustainable revenue and respond to emerging public health priorities.
  • Cultivate and sustain relationships with federal and state agencies, philanthropic funders, community and field partners, and other organizations; develop these relationships into opportunities for new and expanded work;represent EDC in external discussions and forumsto strengthen MCHsystems.
  • In coordination with the Director of Maternal and Child Health, shape business development strategies, concepts, proposals, and partnership approaches, drawing on established networks and EDC expertise to build durable new areas of MCH work. Build and qualify a pipeline of opportunities, develop capture and proposal strategies, and help secure new funding across public and philanthropic sources.
  • Provide strategic oversight of complex, large-scale MCH projects and initiatives; help project leaders align workplans, staffing, deliverables, quality, and funder expectations with the goals of the MCH area of focus and EDC’s broader strategy.
  • Collaborate with project directors and multidisciplinary teams across EDC to lead high-quality delivery, partnerships, and business development.
  • Apply a broad public health perspective, including relevant MCH policy, financing, and systems considerations, to identify strategic opportunities and guide EDC’s response to emerging priorities. Translate policy and financing developments into actionable strategies, fundable initiatives, and partnership opportunities.
    • Contribute to national thought leadership through presentations, convenings, publications, and strategic partnerships and connect our work to the priorities of funders, policymakers, and the MCH field.

Education

  • Master’s degree or equivalent combination of training & experience required in a related discipline
  • PhD desirable

Skills & Experience

  • 12+ years related experience in maternal and child health or related public health field, with 5+ years of complex project management experience, including budget responsibility and staff supervision
  • Demonstrated experience leading or providing senior oversight for complex, large-scale MCH or related public health initiatives, including work with multiple partners and funders.
  • An established professional network and demonstrated ability to represent an organization credibly with public agencies, funders, partners, and the broader MCH field and to use those relationships to advance strategic partnerships and impact MCH systems.
  • Strong understanding of MCH systems and the public health landscape; experience in MCH policy, health financing, or related systems-level work is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated financial and operational management skills, including forecasting, budget oversight, risk management, and resource allocation across multiple related projects and initiatives.
  • Experience coaching and supervising project leaders and multidisciplinary teams, with the ability to foster accountability, collaboration, and high-quality performance.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills, including the ability to translate complex technical and strategic issues for varied audiences.
  • Excellent analytical skills and aptitude for details

Highly Preferred

  • Recognized expertise and professional credibility in MCH or a related public health field, with an established network and the demonstrated ability to represent an organization, build trust, and influence among agencies, funders, partners, and national field audiences to advance strategic partnerships and strengthen MCH systems
  • A track record of business development success, including cultivating opportunities, building and qualifying an opportunity pipeline, developing capture strategies,shaping competitive proposals, developing partnerships, and generating or securing new funding.
  • Experience cultivating philanthropic or foundation relationships and developing fundable initiatives aligned with funder priorities and organizational strengths.

Travel

  • Ability to travel 1 - 2 days per month

EDC affirms its steadfast commitment to uphold the highest standards of conduct, ensuring the protection of all individuals from misconduct, and maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards any violation of these rights. Safeguarding refers to the measures and practices put in place to protect individuals, particularly vulnerable groups, from harm, abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship. At this time, the EDC is unable to support employment-based visa sponsorship.

EDC is a smoke-free workplace, and offers a supportive work environment, competitive salary, and excellent benefits.

Total Rewards:

EDC offers the following comprehensive benefits package for all eligible employees:

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid holidays
  • Generous vacation benefits for full- and part-time employees
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Pre-tax transport benefit
  • Robust retirement plan with TIAA/CREF (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association/College Retirement Equities Fund)
  • Paid sick time and personal time annually
  • Parental leave
  • Employee assistance program

The starting base salary range for this position is $120,000 - $165,000.

If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran, you have the right to request accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access the EDC job opportunities website as a result of your disability. You can request reasonable accommodations by e-mailing  or by calling 202.572.3781.

Education Development Center (EDC) is a global nonprofit that works with partners to advance every person’s journey to learn, work, and be well. For more than 65 years, EDC has partnered with communities, governments, and private sector to improve education, workforce development and health outcomes.

By combining interdisciplinary expertise with real-world experience, EDC works across these pillars to design, implement, and scale evidence-based solutions that help partners address complex challenges and create lasting change.

Founded in 1958, EDC today brings together a global team working across the United States and around the world. Our diverse portfolio of programs is supported by federal agencies, philanthropic foundations, multilateral institutions, and corporate partners.

Job brief

Join Elite Escapes and turn your passion for travel into your next career.

As a Remote Cruise Planner (Sales-Focused),

you'll help clients turn we should take a cruise someday into a confirmed sailing they cannot wait to board. You'll combine destination knowledge, great service, and a consultative sales approach to match travelers with the right ship, itinerary, cabin, and onboard experience—whether they are planning a romantic escape, multigenerational family vacation, celebration at sea, group sailing, or bucket-list voyage.

What You'll Do

  • Connect with clients to understand their preferred destinations, travel style, budget, dates, group size, and cruise must-haves.
  • Recommend the right cruise line, ship, itinerary, stateroom, dining package, shore excursions, and add-ons based on each traveler's needs.
  • Turn inquiries into confirmed cruise vacations through email, chat, and phone with energy, accuracy, and a client-first approach.
  • Explain cruise options clearly, including cabin categories, deposits, payment plans, travel protection, onboard packages, and port requirements.
  • Handle booking details, special requests, changes, payments, upgrades, and pre-cruise questions with professionalism and care.
  • Resolve concerns quickly and confidently, helping clients feel supported from their first quote through embarkation and their return home.
  • Share valuable cruise insights—best sailings for families, romantic itineraries, hidden-gem ports, seasonal opportunities, and limited-time promotions.
  • Build post-booking relationships that encourage repeat sailings, referrals, reviews, and long-term client loyalty.

Nice to Have

  • Interest in cruises, ocean travel, river cruising, expedition voyages, or helping people explore the world by sea.
  • Travel-industry, sales, hospitality, customer-service, or booking experience is preferred—but not required. Zero experience is welcome.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to guide clients toward a decision.
  • Strong organization skills and comfort managing multiple quotes, reservations, follow-ups, and client details.
  • Comfort with technology, online booking platforms, CRM systems, and AI tools—we will train you on the rest.
  • A genuine passion for travel, memorable experiences, and helping clients find the cruise that feels made for them.

What You Get

  • Fully remote work with the flexibility to build your schedule around your life.
  • Comprehensive onboarding and training on cruise lines, ships, itineraries, supplier platforms, sales conversations, and travel planning.
  • A collaborative, supportive team atmosphere with colleagues who want to see you succeed.
  • The opportunity to grow into specialties such as luxury cruises, family cruising, group sailings, river cruises, expedition travel, or destination celebrations.
  • Clear paths toward leadership and higher earning potential.

Cruise planning has plenty of moving parts—but if you enjoy helping people choose between ocean views and balconies, island stops and bucket-list ports, relaxation and adventure, you will thrive here. Your work will transform questions into bookings and cruise dreams into unforgettable days at sea.

Who We Are

We curate journeys that turn travel dreams into reality. We believe travel and adventure should create transformative, lifelong memories — that's why we partner with advisors who share that passion.

Apply today—we look forward to welcoming you aboard.

jobs.description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:


We’re seeking a Senior Associate to join an impact-oriented team focused on improving accuracy, reducing friction, and strengthening the integrity of our end-to-end claims adjudication processes. The team partners closely with Operations, Product, and Engineering to identify breakdowns, uncover patterns, and maintain strong operations across the organization.


In this role, you will work through operational queues of claims, investigating and resolving each one with rigor and curiosity. Blending thoughtful analysis and pattern recognition, you will recognize when an issue points to a broader problem and escalate it to help build durable fixes. You will have the opportunity to build deep expertise in our claims operations, and help leverage AI agents and LLM-powered tools.


Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

  • Work through designated queues of claims with high attention to detail, identifying and correcting errors while ensuring well-supported and clearly documented determinations
  • Investigate claim errors, recognizing when individual errors or anomalies point to broader themes, trends, or systemic issues and escalating them as needed with clear context

jobs.description:
About TTS-US:

Founded in 2011, Toyota Tsusho Systems US, Inc. (TTS-US) is a Toyota group company, that develops IT solutions wherever global businesses operate. Transforming into a technology and mobility company, TTS-US with it's 8 TTS affiliates worldwide is establishing a secure and resilient Toyota global value chain. The creative capacity to forge such limitless business opportunities is one of the strengths of Toyota Tsusho Systems.

Summary:

The Product Cybersecurity Group is building an AI harness that brings Generative and agentic AI capabilities to Product Cybersecurity engineering. The Principal AI Security Software Engineer works hands-on with the team, building the prompts, agents, tools, connectors, and workflows that make AI perform real Product Cybersecurity work across PCG workflows and customer environments.

This is a hands-on engineering role. The Principal AI Security Software Engineer spends most of their time writing, testing, and shipping code alongside the team, rather than producing architecture documents for others to implement. This role does not train foundation models. Instead, the engineer takes existing models and makes them perform useful, reliable, measurable work by building the full path from prototype to production, including the data access, orchestration, evaluation, and observability that make AI features trustworthy enough for use in security-sensitive environments.

The Principal AI Security Software Engineer brings a software developer's mindset to AI, including version control, code review, testing, debugging, and maintainable design. The engineer works as part of the team, partnering with engineers, turning security tasks into working AI-assisted workflows, and helping team members learn to build and extend those workflows themselves.

Essential Functions:

· Build (the majority of the role)

o Write and ship the components that make AI do the work — prompts, agents, skills, tools, MCP servers, connectors, scripts, and orchestration logic — assembled into end-to-end LLM applications such as retrieval pipelines, agent workflows, and structured-output workflows

o Turn the team's manual security tasks into working AI-assisted workflows, such as engineering analysis, knowledge retrieval, documentation, requirements analysis, code/design review, test generation, and security-assessment support

o Securely connect the harness to approved customer documentation, knowledge sources, repositories, APIs, identity systems, and downstream tools so AI operates with relevant context

o Build a reusable library of components so each new use case is faster to deliver than the last

· Shape the technical approach

o Make and document practical design decisions for the harness — model integration, context management, tool integration — so the team can build on them

o Contribute design and code reviews that keep components maintainable, secure, and reusable

o Recommend when to build, reuse, or stop an approach based on evidence from working implementations

· Measure

o Build evaluations and quality gates for the workflows you ship — covering output quality, groundedness, hallucination rate, reliability, security, usefulness, latency, and cost — so releases rest on evidence rather than demo impressions

o Analyze production transcripts and user feedback to drive iterative improvement

· Operate

o Version, test, deploy, monitor, and maintain prompts, context, and components with the same discipline as any other code

o Design for reliability — provider or model fallback, graceful degradation, timeouts, and retries — and treat inference cost and latency as first-class constraints

o Implement security practices — access controls, data handling, traceability, guardrails — aligned with internal and customer requirements, and release changes through existing change-management and security review processes

· Work with the Team

o Pair with team members and customer engineers to understand their work, identify the highest-value tasks for AI, and build solutions together

o Help define what AI should and should not be used for, explaining technical constraints in terms non-specialists can act on

o Teach by building: write clear examples, document how components work, and help engineers create and extend their own AI workflows

Competencies:

  • Advanced software engineering and application development expertise.
  • Strong knowledge of Generative AI, agentic AI systems, prompt engineering, context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and LLM application development.
  • Ability to evaluate, troubleshoot, and improve complex AI-enabled workflows using measurable performance criteria.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and mentor engineers through hands-on development and knowledge sharing.
  • Demonstrated critical thinking, innovation, sound judgment, and the ability to solve complex technical problems in security-sensitive environments.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of professional software development experience, with a track record of personally writing, shipping, and maintaining production software.
  • Solid software engineering fundamentals: version control, code review, automated testing, debugging, and maintainable design.
  • Hands-on experience building LLM-powered applications or AI-assisted workflows, including prompting and context engineering, retrieval (RAG), agent and tool-use frameworks, and evaluation; production experience strongly preferred.
  • Practical experience with model APIs from at least one major provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or an open-weight equivalent).
  • Cloud experience (AWS, Azure, or GCP), containerization, and CI/CD.
  • Experience designing secure systems: access controls, data handling, traceability, and guardrails for sensitive data.
  • Ability to reason rigorously about non-deterministic systems and understand why a passing demo is not equivalent to a passing test.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; able to explain tradeoffs to engineers and executives alike.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building agentic AI systems: tool usage, workflow orchestration, multi-step autonomous workflows, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
  • Experience with MCP, agent orchestration frameworks, and observability/tracing for LLM applications.
  • Background in Product Cybersecurity, application security, or security-assessment workflows.
  • Experience defining evaluation frameworks for AI output quality, reliability, and safety.
  • Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps practices for versioning, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining AI systems.
  • Familiarity with AI governance and risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act) and secure handling of sensitive data in AI systems.
  • Experience running technical workshops, pairing, or mentoring engineers new to AI.

ST. CHARLES HEALTH SYSTEM

JOB DESCRIPTION


TITLE: Charge Capture Specialist II

REPORTS TO POSITION: Revenue Integrity Leadership

DEPARTMENT: Revenue Integrity Department

DATE LAST REVIEWED: 11/10/2026


OUR VISION: Creating America’s healthiest community, together

OUR MISSION: In the spirit of love and compassion, better health, better care, better value

OUR VALUES: Accountability, Caring and Teamwork


DEPARTMENT SUMMARY: The Revenue Integrity department focuses on charge capture optimization and documentation improvement through collaboration and education. The Revenue Integrity department provides many services to our multi-hospital and medical group organization focusing on the patient financial experience along the entire continuum of care. Our goal is to deliver delightful, transparent, and seamless experience to our patients and customers that captures and collects the revenue earned by St. Charles Health System (SCHS) in a quality, efficient and timely manner.


POSITION OVERVIEW: The Charge Capture Specialist II at SCHS is responsible for validating appropriate charge capture in a quality, efficient and timely manner. Services include but are not limited to the review of accounts to accurately capture charges for assigned Charge Capture Area and other SCHS departments and or cost centers as applicable. This role requires the ability to review medical record documentation to apply accurate charges for services and items/supplies used for patient care, perform basic math and/or time calculations and correct charge capture errors based on SCHS charge capture policies and procedures. This position does not directly manage others but may be asked to review and provide feedback on other caregiver’s work, as well as support other Revenue Integrity Charge Capture Specialist’s with daily work activities.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS:

Read and interpret documents contained within the medical record.


Accurately determine the charges for the assigned services departments, transferring data to Information Services and Finance as scheduled.


Complete accurate and timely charge capture tasks for assigned Charge Capture Area.


Deliver excellent customer service in a manner that promotes goodwill, is timely, efficient and accurate when communication between internal/external stakeholders is necessary according to the RI Charge Capture Complexity Matrix.


Contribute to and support team in assigned work queue areas designated by leadership.


Utilize intermediate to high level research methodologies consistent with the RI Charge Capture Complexity Matrix.


Apply intermediate to high level understanding and knowledge of billing, medical coding and charging guidelines when CPT code(s) application is required following Medicare/Medicaid/Payor guidelines, Federal and State regulations and or laws along with SCHS policies and procedures for appropriate charge capture processes.


Attend applicable meetings as requested by leadership. Provide requested deliverables as deemed appropriate by leadership.


Support the vision, mission, and values of the organization in all respects.


Support Lean principles of continuous improvement with energy and enthusiasm, functioning as a champion of change.


Provide and maintain a safe environment for caregivers, patients and guests.


Conduct all activities with the highest standards of professionalism and confidentiality. Comply with all applicable laws, regulations, policies and procedures, supporting the organization’s corporate integrity efforts by acting in an ethical and appropriate manner, reporting known or suspected violation of applicable rules, and cooperating fully with all organizational investigations and proceedings.


May perform additional duties of similar complexity within the organization as required or assigned.


EDUCATION:

Required: High School Diploma/GED.

Preferred: Associate or bachelor’s degree in an accredited Health Information Technology program or certification in a self-study course from AHIMA, AAPC, Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT) certification or one or more of the following: RHIA, CCA, CCS, CCS-P, CPC, CPC-H, preferred.


LICENSURE/CERTIFICATION/REGISTRATION

Required: N/A

Preferred: Must hold 2 of the following certifications for certification pay: Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT), RHIA, CHRI, CDIP, CPMA, CCA, CBC, CCS, CCS-P, CPC, CPC-H, CIRCC, preferred.


EXPERIENCE

Required: Two (2) years Revenue Cycle Charge Capture experience required. Related healthcare experience of which one year must have been in a revenue cycle or equivalent role.

Preferred: Three (3) years coding and/or medical billing/collections experience with a Health Information Management focus. Over two years Epic or other EHR experience.


ADDITIONAL POSITION INFORMATION/SKILLS/ABILITIES

Strong interpersonal and communication skills, analytic and organizational skills, critical –thinking and the ability to meet deadlines.

Intermediate to high level proficiency and ability in computer applications, including but not limited to electronic medical record(s), MS Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, and Outlook), Windows operating system and Internet.

Intermediate to high level knowledge of medical billing, coding and charge capture including but not limited to CMS billing and medical coding guidelines, Federal and State billing and coding guidelines, and insurance payer reimbursement methodologies.

Intermediate to high level understanding of CPT-4 code assignment, ICD-10-CM, and ICD-10-PCS code assignment.

Intermediate level understanding of NCCI and medical necessity edits and payment methodologies.

Intermediate knowledge and usage of internal software research tools relating to modifier and revenue code assignment.

Intermediate to high level ability to problem-solving and high-level research skills.

Maintain professional knowledge by attending educational workshops, reviewing professional publications, participating in educational opportunities. Research and present educational opportunities to Supervisor as applicable to role.

Ability to work independently and collaborate with other team members and leaders.
