We are looking for an experienced Senior Customer Success Manager to help our ANZ customers achieve measurable value from Trackunit’s products and services, through a program-based and consultative approach.
You will own an existing local customer base and work largely independently, backed by a global team across Denmark, the Netherlands, Germany, Japan, and beyond. Building and expanding customer partnerships is at the heart of this role, and you will work at the intersection of product innovation, strategic advisory, and change management. You should also be comfortable traveling to customer and partner offices in the ANZ region when needed.

This is a fully remote role based in Australia, however we do have other colleagues around Brisbane.

What’s in it for you?

  • A globally distributed team of engaged colleagues, with regular check-ins and social events across teams and borders.

  • A place in an agile, fast-growing SaaS business with real opportunities to grow internally. We have grown from 150 employees in 2020 to more than 450, so expect pace and change.

  • Genuine flexibility. We are remote-friendly in practice, not just in the job ad. You choose the routine that works best for you, and we provide the IT equipment you need.

  • Development that is taken seriously: training, coaching, mindfulness, and an open feedback culture focused on your impact on yourself, your teams and relationships, and the organisation.

  • Turning the Tide. We are committed to an inclusive workplace, starting with hiring. We do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status, and we assess candidates only on qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and our other DE&I initiativeshere.

Who are you ideally?

  • You have proven experience in Customer Success, or a similar customer-facing role, managing a portfolio proactively. Experience level: 5 to 10+ years, ideally in SaaS, IoT, telematics, or within the construction or equipment industry.

  • You have a track record of working independently and fully remotely: you structure your own time, make sound decisions without constant guidance, and know when to pull in colleagues.

  • You build strong relationships, including with senior and executive stakeholders.

  • You have analytical and troubleshooting skills, plus the patience and perseverance to see complex issues through.

  • You communicate clearly and positively, turning complex challenges into simple next steps.

  • You deliver quality across multiple accounts under tight deadlines.

  • You bring curiosity and a collaborative mindset in an international team where everyone is learning.

Bonus points for experience in construction, equipment rental, or OEM and dealer environments, or experience working with partners or distribution channels.
Don’t meet every requirement? That is fine. If you are excited about this role but your experience does not tick every box, we encourage you to apply.

Primary responsibilities

  • Be the voice of the customer and their trusted advisor across the full lifecycle, from onboarding and adoption to renewal and expansion.

  • Own the relationship as the designated point of contact for your portfolio, with full responsibility for customer health and outcomes.

  • Set up and run regular cadence calls and Executive Business Reviews that tie Trackunit’s value to customers’ business goals.

  • Proactively manage risks, issues, and escalations, keeping internal and external stakeholders aligned and customers informed about upcoming releases.

  • Analyse usage data and customer feedback to drive adoption and continuous improvement, and feed insights back to Product and other teams.

  • Share best practices and lead training sessions and workshops.

  • Build strong relationships with our partners and stakeholders in the region.

Our hiring process
Don’t waste your time on writing the best possible cover letter for the job. We want you to create an impact that matters, and that’s not in the cover letter.

  • Virtual meet and greet. Meet with the Talent Acquisition Partner.

  • A deeper conversation: We’ll go into your experience and how you work, and you’ll get a clearer picture of the team, the challenges, and what the role actually looks like day to day.

  • Assignment-specific interview. We want you to get an insight into some of the concrete work tasks or projects related to the role. You will be given a case to prepare prior to the interview, and at the interview, you will present the case to relevant colleagues from across Trackunit, who you’ll also work closely with in the job.

  • If needed, throughout the process we will obtain references from former employers and do background checks for level specific, if you have not provided these yourself.

  • Offer presentation and walk-through. We’re lucky to have you!

Coming Together To Connect Construction

Construction is one of the largest industries in the world, and for two decades Trackunit has pioneered technological progress within it. Today we are a leading IoT provider and a thought leader, helping drive the agenda for the whole industry.
We take a people-first approach in everything we do, in our products and in how we work. Our colleagues gather in hubs around the globe, and we embrace working remotely in environments that inspire you. Everything we do is to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry in the world.

The question is: are you in?

At LanguageLine, we strive for a world in which language and cultural barriers no longer exist. Use your language skills to dramatically improve the lives of limited-English speakers, as well as the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing. Even better, you can do this while working from your own home.

You'll also be supported by a Senior Language Specialist, as well as our Interpreter and Technology Help Desks.

Join our team now!

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Hebrew-English Video-Phone Interpreter


Job Title: Hebrew Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Video-Phone Interpreter

Pay: $15 - $17 per hour.

  • Compensation will not be less than any applicable state or local minimum wage.
    • For Colorado applicants, the expected pay range is $15.16 - $19.29 per hour.

We Offer:

  • Paid professional interpreter training and continuous development.
  • Incentives for meeting attendance targets.
  • Benefits include: Paid Sick Leave in accordance with applicable law, Medical, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Accident, Critical Illness & Life, AD&D, Insurance Package, Inpatient Hospital, Short Term Disability, and 401K Retirement.
  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.

Position Overview:


The Hebrew Video-Telephone- Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Hebrew and English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.


The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The video and audio interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.


This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The interpreters translate verbally.


**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment**


Essential Job Functions:

  • Respond to video and audio interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Participate in online, video and audio training sessions.
  • Deliver interpretation services via video and expediently type data on a dedicated device, such as a laptop, desktop computer, mobile phone, or tablet, in order to perform the essential functions of the job.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the video and audio interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during video and audio interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during scheduled work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency inHebrew and English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages – highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**


Technical Requirements:

  • Dedicated personal device for business purposes.
    • Desktop / Laptop Computers with any of the following Operating Systems: Windows, MacOS, or ChromeOS.
    • Tablets (iPadOS or Android) are acceptable.
    • Smartphones (iOS or Android) are also acceptable.
  • Restricted brands:
    • Kaspersky products.
    • Huawei hardware.
  • High speed Internet connection for work related electronic communication. This internet connection should provide download speeds of no less than 5 Mbps, upload speeds of 3 Mbps, Ping value of no more than 300 ms, Jitter value of no more than 30 ms.

Vill du vara med och förändra vården?

Då vill vi prata med dig!

Om den digitala tjänsten

Hej! Jag heter Maria Lundqvist och är verksamhetschef på Kry Digital. Jag tror på en enkel sak: vården blir bättre när vi vågar göra den annorlunda. I vår digitala tjänst jobbar vi nära varandra med hjälp av våra digitala verktyg. Det är lika självklart att be om hjälp som att komma med en ny idé. Vi är ett team på 140 medarbetare som delar samma övertygelse – att hög tillgänglighet, ny teknik och ett genuint fokus på kvalitet och patientnöjdhet inte är motsatser. Det bevisar vi varje dag.

Varför Kry?
Vi har förändrat hur vård bedrivs i Sverige i över tio år. Gjort den digital, tillgänglig och mer jämlik. Men vi är inte klara och det är poängen.På Kry tror vi att det modigaste du kan göra i vårdbranschen är att vara snäll. Och att de som kan vården ska styra den. Hos oss får du mandat att göra det - ta det, be inte om det.

Vad du faktiskt gör

Du genomför digitala konsultationer via vår plattform och du gör det på ett sätt som får patienter att känna sig sedda. Du kommer även arbeta direkt avlastande mot våra vårdcentraler och du kommer att arbeta i lokala journalsystem. Arbetet är brett. Du utreder, bedömer och behandlar patienter i alla åldrar: akuta bedömningar, långsiktig uppföljning, digitalt och fysiskt. Du samarbetar nära vårdcentralerna och övriga vårdflöden. Vi tror inte att digital och fysisk vård är varandras motpoler. De är varandras förutsättningar. Dina erfarenheter är med och formar hur vi arbetar, idag och framåt. Det kallar vi Kry-modellen.Läs mer om den här.

Vad vi förväntar oss av dig

  • Du är allmänspecialist eller ST inom allmänmedicin med minst 2 års erfarenhet från vårdcentral.

  • Du tar ansvar och får saker gjorda.

  • Du trivs i förändring och ser det som kul.

  • Du levererar vård med hög kvalitet och sätter patienten först.

  • Du är flytande i både svenska och engelska.

  • Meriterande med erfarenhet av Cosmic, Take Care eller PMO.

Praktiskt

Start: Höst/vinter 2026

Ersättning:Timlön eller konsultarvode

Arbetstid:Vardagar dagtid, kvällar efter 19 samt helg

Är du redo?

Skicka din ansökan senast 30/11 2026. Vid eventuella frågor, vänligen ämnesraden "Rekrytering läkare".

Vi ser fram emot att höra från dig!

Ta hand om dig ❤

jobs.description:
The Senior Product Designer owns the end-to-end user experience of Acumatica applications, shapes workflows, and aligns them with the product vision. As an active member of the discovery team, they collaborate with the Product Manager, Business Analyst, Engineering Lead, and backend developers to translate business requirements into validated, scalable solutions. This role includes building working prototypes for Business Analysts to specify from and for backend developers to connect services to, modeling system behavior, writing clear behavioral specifications for engineers and AI agents, and ensuring AI-generated output meets quality and accessibility standards. The Senior Product Designer also mentors team members, leads cross-functional design sprints, and links design work to measurable business outcomes.

MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Discovery & Validation: Understanding Users and Problems

  • Conduct and synthesize user research and competitive analysis, including emerging UX patterns and AI capabilities, to inform design direction

  • Validate early concepts with users through working prototypes before committing to full design or engineering effort

  • Lead usability and UX acceptance testing to ensure the experience functions as designed. Define success metrics such as task completion, error rate, CSAT, and adoption with product managers. Identify and raise UX defects before release.

Interactive Systems Design: Designing Behavior, Not Just Screens

  • Own end-to-end UX for assigned epics, including AI-surfaced and headless experiences. Partner with the Engineering Lead to assess feasibility and trade-offs.

  • Model user flows, screen and component states, and transitions, defining how the UI responds to user input, validation, system events, and API responses

  • Design for non-deterministic AI output by defining fallback, recovery, and human-in-the-loop behavior when results are incomplete, incorrect, or low confidence

Prototype & Behavioral Specification: Building the Working Reference

  • Build working code prototypes in the component library to serve as reference artifacts. These prototypes help Business Analysts write functional and business specifications and enable backend developers to connect real services.

  • Structure prototypes to be plug-in ready, with defined mock data structures and clear data shapes. Keep the UI separate from data logic to prevent backend rework.

  • Write behavioral specifications that AI coding agents can interpret clearly, covering interaction rules, states, edge cases, and UI acceptance criteria.

  • Define UI-level guardrails for AI-surfaced features, such as how uncertainty is displayed, when human confirmation is required, and how users can override. Partner with the Product Manager and Business Analyst to establish the supporting business rules.

  • Annotate prototypes with known business rules and open questions to surface rules that do not appear on screen, such as permissions, validation logic, and calculations, early in the process.

  • Build reusable specification templates, prompt templates, and context files to ensure AI-generated output remains consistent with the design system.

Design Systems & Versioning: Keeping Design and Code in Sync

  • Work directly in BitBucket repositories: create branches, commit changes, open and review pull requests, and resolve basic merge conflicts

  • Store and edit design tokens in the code repository, keeping Figma variables and coded tokens aligned

  • Treat the coded component library as the source of truth, moving beyond Figma-only handoff. Structure the system so AI agents can use it reliably.

AI-Assisted Workflows & Design QA: Building Fast, Shipping Right

  • Use AI tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Figma Make) to build working prototypes in hours rather than days

  • Coordinate AI agents for research synthesis, specification drafting, prototyping, and documentation, while maintaining responsibility for final design decisions.

  • Audit AI-generated code and UI for design system compliance, interaction accuracy, and accessibility before it reaches engineering or users

  • 5+ years of product design experience, with demonstrated impact on shipped products and business outcomes

  • Portfolio showing end-to-end ownership of complex B2B or enterprise workflows, including state models, edge cases, and system behavior

  • Demonstrate the ability to build working code prototypes with AI-assisted tools that Business Analysts can specify from and backend developers can connect services to, using defined mock data and UI separated from data logic.

  • Demonstrate strong accessibility awareness by applying WCAG standards and understanding assistive technologies to ensure all users can engage with the product effectively.

  • Demonstrate fluency in designing screen- and flow-level patterns for AI-surfaced and agentic experiences, including confidence indicators, override affordances, and human-in-the-loop controls, across both visual and headless interfaces.

  • Apply AI-augmented design strategy by setting cross-feature principles for how AI appears in the product (trust, transparency, user control, and communicating uncertainty), partnering with Data and AI teams, and guiding how AI is used across the design workflow

  • Connect design decisions to business goals, contributing to and constructively challenging product direction from a design perspective.

  • Apply systems thinking by designing for scale and long-term impact and understanding how individual features integrate into the overall product ecosystem.

  • Communicate design rationale confidently to team members, contribute actively to cross-functional meetings, and build strong relationships across functions.

  • Demonstrate facilitation skills by leading workshops and cross-functional sessions, knowing when to guide, when to step back, and how to move a group from divergence to decision.

  • Exhibit sound judgment and leadership when navigating ambiguity without clear precedent, taking ownership of outcomes rather than just outputs.

jobs.title: Sales Manager — United Kingdom
jobs.excerpt: About Founda HealthFounda Health operates a healthcare interoperability platform that lets hospitals, health information exchanges, clinics, digital health applications, PACS and EHRs exchange data through open standards — IHE, HL7, FHIR and DICOM.
jobs.description:
About Founda Health

Founda Health operates a healthcare interoperability platform that lets hospitals, health information exchanges, clinics, digital health applications, PACS and EHRs exchange data through open standards — IHE, HL7, FHIR and DICOM. Our mission is to dramatically improve the quality and efficiency of healthcare by commoditizing healthcare data availability across the ecosystem.

The platform runs on two complementary stacks. XDS, our document and image exchange core, was acquired from Philips and serves more than 50 customers across the Netherlands, Germany and beyond. The Health Platform and FHIR CDR is our modern API layer, connecting digital health applications and data consumers — GPs, AI companies, research, payers — to legacy healthcare data. We are the only vendor combining proven XDS document and image exchange with a modern FHIR layer; competitors have one or the other.

Our positioning: Founda delivers radical simplicity in healthcare data exchange, empowering every actor in the ecosystem to focus on outcomes — not infrastructure. We are the open, vendor-agnostic alternative, with an AI-ready architecture.

Founda is Amsterdam-headquartered, remote-first, The Netherlands and Germany are our core markets; the UK is an active expansion market.

Why this role exists

Founda has a proven platform and a strong European footprint, but no senior commercial presence inside the UK public sector. The NHS does not buy interoperability the way a Dutch or German hospital group does: requirements are shaped through national programmes, shared care record strategies, clinical safety and standards assurance, and framework agreements — usually long before anything reaches a tender portal. By the time a specification is published, the outcome is often already decided.

We are hiring someone to be in those rooms early. This person represents Founda at central government, NHS England and trust level, builds the relationships that give us visibility into what is coming, and shapes specifications, frameworks and procurement routes so that the ground we bid on fits a standards-based, vendor-agnostic platform. They then convert that position into signed business against their own number.

There is no existing UK team, no inherited pipeline and no established brand recognition with NHS buyers. The right candidate sees that as the attraction.

Core responsibilities

Shaping the market before the tender

  • Build and hold Founda's relationships at national level — central government health digital policy, NHS England and relevant arm's-length bodies, and the national programmes that set direction for data sharing.

  • Track policy, consultations, standards work and funding announcements, and translate them into a view of where the buying will happen over the next 12 to 36 months.

  • Influence specifications, framework scopes and procurement routes ahead of formal competition, so that open, standards-based interoperability is the shape of the requirement.

  • Secure Founda's position on the procurement routes UK health bodies actually buy through — national and regional framework agreements, dynamic markets under the Procurement Act 2023, and direct award routes where they apply.

Winning business

  • Own the UK public sector pipeline end to end: identify and qualify ICBs, trusts and national bodies, run the full cycle through to contract signature and handover to delivery, against an individual quota.

  • Lead complex, multi-stakeholder pursuits involving clinical, digital, information governance, procurement and finance stakeholders — and the incumbent suppliers already embedded in the account.

  • Run competitive bids and tender responses, coordinating the internal contributors a credible NHS submission needs.

  • Negotiate and commit commercial terms within agreed pricing bands; anything outside band goes to the CCO.

Defining how Founda sells into the UK

  • Own the UK public sector go-to-market approach — qualification criteria, segmentation, partner and channel choices, bid/no-bid discipline and the commercial patterns that work in this market.

  • Be the recognised internal authority on UK public sector: the person Product, Marketing, Delivery and leadership come to before committing anything UK-specific.

  • Feed what you hear in policy and procurement back into Product, pricing and delivery planning so the roadmap reflects real UK requirements rather than assumptions.

  • Maintain an accurate pipeline and forecast in HubSpot that leadership can plan against.

Representing Founda

  • Act as Founda's face in the UK market — at NHS and health-tech events, in standards and interoperability communities, and with the partner ecosystem.

  • Work alongside Solution Architects, Customer Success, Product, Legal and Marketing so that what is promised commercially holds up technically and contractually.

  • Mentor more junior commercial colleagues as the UK presence grows, without line management responsibility.

What this role is not

Worth being explicit, so we screen for the right person:

  • Not a people management role. There are no direct reports and no team to build in year one. Candidates whose next step must be a leadership title are not the right fit.

  • Not a pure public affairs or policy role. Influence is the method; signed revenue is the outcome. The person carries a number.

  • Not a global business development role. Opening new countries, and global technology alliances, sit with our EVP Business Development. This role is the UK, in depth.

  • Not a transactional or high-volume sales role. Expect long, consultative public sector cycles with many stakeholders, not monthly close rates.

  • Not a roadmap-committing role. Product commitments are made by Product and the CCO. This person shapes them with market evidence; they do not promise features in a bid.

Experience we are looking for

Essential

  • A demonstrable, current NHS network at senior level — named relationships at NHS trusts, ICBs, NHS England or central government health digital bodies that the candidate can describe concretely.

  • A track record of selling complex technology into the UK public health sector, with evidence of deals personally led from origination to signature.

  • Genuine command of NHS and UK public sector procurement: framework agreements, dynamic markets and the Procurement Act 2023, clinical safety and assurance expectations, and how business cases actually get approved inside a trust or ICB.

  • Experience influencing requirements before a tender is issued, not only responding to one — and able to give examples.

  • Comfort with the technical substance of healthcare interoperability: standards-based data exchange, integration with EHR and PACS estates, and why architectural choices matter to a buyer.

  • Carried and hit an individual quota in an enterprise or public sector context.

  • Able to operate as the only person in a market, in a remote-first company, with the self-direction that requires.

Strongly preferred

  • Working knowledge of FHIR, HL7, DICOM, IHE or XDS, and of NHS standards and assurance expectations such as FHIR UK Core, SNOMED-CT and DCB0129 / DCB0160 clinical risk management.

  • Familiarity with shared care records, regional imaging and data-sharing programmes, and the suppliers already embedded in them.

  • Experience at a scale-up or challenger vendor competing against entrenched incumbents, rather than only at a large established supplier.

  • An existing presence in UK health-tech and interoperability communities — speaking, standards participation, or a recognised professional profile.

Nice to have

  • Experience in the devolved nations (Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland) alongside NHS England.

  • Exposure to European health data regulation and how it is influencing UK suppliers and buyers.

  • Prior first-hire or market-entry experience for a non-UK vendor.

What good looks like

First 3 months

Mapped the UK landscape — priority trusts, ICBs, national programmes, incumbents and partners. Reactivated or built a first tier of senior relationships. Formed a clear point of view on where Founda can win and where we should not play.

6 months

About the Role

We are seeking a customer-focused Level 1 Application Support Analyst with hands-on experience supporting Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 and working knowledge of Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O).

In this role, you will provide first-line functional and technical application support, troubleshoot incidents, monitor critical business processes, and help maintain the smooth operation of enterprise applications.

You will work closely with experienced Level 2 and Level 3 consultants, taking ownership of support requests, resolving issues within agreed service levels, and escalating complex technical problems with appropriate diagnostic information.

The ideal candidate will have a solid understanding of Microsoft Dynamics ERP environments, strong troubleshooting capabilities, and a proactive, customer-centric approach to application support.

About the Client

You will be supporting a large Australian healthcare organisation operating within a complex enterprise technology environment. The organisation relies on Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012, Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, and Azure-based integrations to support critical business operations.

You will collaborate with experienced technical consultants and internal stakeholders to ensure reliable application performance and a high standard of support for business users.

Ideal Profile

Microsoft Dynamics Experience

  • Minimum of 2 years of hands-on functional or technical support experience with Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 (R2 or R3) in a production environment.
  • Working knowledge of Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, including system navigation, batch jobs, security roles, and Data Management Framework (DMF).
  • Strong understanding of core ERP business processes, including:
    • General Ledger (GL)
    • Accounts Payable (AP)
    • Accounts Receivable (AR)
    • Procurement and Purchase Order Management
    • Inventory and Warehouse Management.

Application Support & Troubleshooting

  • Practical experience monitoring, troubleshooting, and administering Dynamics AX batch jobs.
  • Experience with user administration, access management, and security role configuration within Microsoft Dynamics environments.
  • Familiarity with ITIL-based incident, problem, and service request management processes.
  • Experience using IT service management platforms such as Freshservice, ServiceNow, or equivalent.
  • Ability to interpret application logs, error messages, and technical diagnostic information.
  • Basic SQL knowledge, including executing read-only queries for troubleshooting.

Technical & Integration Knowledge

  • Understanding of application integrations and experience supporting business-critical data flows.
  • Familiarity with Azure-based monitoring and integration technologies.
  • Ability to troubleshoot application issues systematically and identify recurring problems.

Desirable Experience

  • Exposure to Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) processes and troubleshooting.
  • Experience supporting ERP integrations involving external suppliers and third-party systems.
  • Familiarity with Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, and Logic Apps.
  • Experience with Grafana, Orion, or similar enterprise monitoring platforms.
  • Exposure to handheld devices and mobile applications used in warehouse or inventory operations.
  • Experience supporting healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, distribution, or other regulated industries.
  • Understanding of Dynamics 365 F&O Data Management Framework (DMF).
  • Microsoft Dynamics certifications such as MB-300 or MB-310.
  • ITIL 4 Foundation certification.

Qualifications & Professional Capabilities

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Commerce, Accounting, or a related discipline. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Customer-focused approach with the ability to provide effective remote application support.
  • Good documentation skills and the ability to collaborate with technical teams and business stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Application Support & Incident Management

  • Provide Level 1 functional and technical support for Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 and Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations.
  • Monitor and manage incoming incidents and service requests through Freshservice or equivalent IT service management platforms.
  • Investigate, diagnose, and resolve application issues in line with established procedures and service level agreements (SLAs).
  • Categorise and prioritise support requests based on business impact, urgency, and severity.
  • Take ownership of assigned incidents through to successful resolution.
  • Escalate complex issues to Level 2 and Level 3 support teams, providing detailed diagnostic information, error messages, and supporting documentation.
  • Maintain accurate ticket records and provide regular updates to end users.

System Monitoring & Operational Support

  • Perform operational health checks across Dynamics AX 2012 and D365 F&O environments.
  • Monitor scheduled batch jobs, background processes, and recurring business operations.
  • Investigate failed or stalled batch jobs and perform approved corrective actions, including restarting or rescheduling processes.
  • Monitor application performance and system alerts using Grafana, Orion, and Azure monitoring services.
  • Identify potential system issues proactively and escalate risks before they affect business operations.
  • Perform routine checks of integration folders, file shares, service accounts, and application dependencies.

Integration & EDI Support

  • Provide first-line monitoring and troubleshooting of integrations between Dynamics AX 2012, D365 F&O, and Azure services.
  • Investigate integration failures involving financial transactions, vendor invoices, customer invoices, and other business-critical data flows.
  • Monitor EDI processes, including purchase orders, invoices, and supplier acknowledgements.
  • Troubleshoot failed integration messages and perform approved reprocessing or resubmission activities.
  • Identify recurring integration failures and escalate patterns for further investigation and root cause analysis.

User Administration & Functional Support

  • Process approved user access requests, including account creation, user deactivation, and security role assignments.
  • Support standard security and access management processes within AX 2012 and D365 F&O.
  • Assist users with application navigation and common functional issues across finance, procurement, and inventory management.
  • Provide first-line troubleshooting for handheld devices and mobile applications used in warehouse and pharmacy operations.
  • Guide users through established procedures and known workarounds to resolve common application issues.

Documentation & Continuous Improvement

  • Create, maintain, and improve standard operating procedures, technical documentation, knowledge articles, and troubleshooting runbooks.
  • Identify recurring incidents and recommend improvements to reduce support ticket volumes.
  • Assist with application testing, release validation, and post-deployment health checks.
  • Contribute to service performance reporting and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate with technical consultants and internal stakeholders to maintain a high-quality application support experience.

How we take care of our team

💰 Get paid in Australian Dollars

🏥 Medical insurance from day one for you + spouse (or parents if unmarried)
🩺 Generous OPD coverage from doctor visits to all your medical needs
🏡 Home office setup allowance to build your ideal workspace

🗣️ Open-door culture – your ideas and feedback always matter

jobs.description:
Team: Product
Reporting to: Senior Director of Product Management
Location: India (Remote)

About ELSA

ELSA is a global leader in AI-powered English communication training, dedicated to transforming how people learn and speak English with confidence. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, we operate across the U.S., Vietnam, Portugal, Indonesia, Brazil and Japan.

Powered by proprietary speech-recognition technology and generative AI, ELSA delivers real-time, hyper-personalized feedback to help learners improve pronunciation, fluency, and overall communication effectiveness. With over 50 million learners and 1 billion hours of anonymized speech data, ELSA's depth of language training intelligence is unmatched in the industry.

Our consumer products help millions of learners build practical English communication skills through personalized, bite-sized learning experiences. ELSA combines AI-powered coaching, speech recognition, adaptive learning, and engaging product experiences to help users build consistent learning habits and make measurable progress.

Our vision is to become the global standard for real-time English communication training, enabling 1.5 billion language learners worldwide to speak clearly, be understood, and share their stories with the world.

Backed by world-class investors including Google's Gradient Ventures, Monk's Hill Ventures, and SOSV, ELSA has been recognized among the top global AI innovators:

  • Forbes Top 4 Companies Using AI to Transform the World

  • Research Sniper Top 5 Best AI Apps

  • ASU+GSV EdTech 150

  • CB Insights Top 100 AI Companies

We are scaling aggressively on the consumer side — moving from a language-learning app into a highly personalized AI communication coach that users build into their daily lives. That means stronger engagement loops, smarter personalization, better learning outcomes, and a product experience that drives long-term retention and subscription growth.

Join us in shaping the future of language learning and empowering millions to unlock opportunity through confident communication.

Job Overview

As Principal Product Manager, B2C, you will set the product vision and strategy for ELSA's consumer business, the experience that millions of learners use to improve their English with AI. You will own the full consumer journey, from discovery and onboarding to lasting learning habits, subscription and long-term retention, and you will be accountable for the metrics that drive B2C growth and revenue.

This is a senior, high-leverage role. You will shape a multi-year roadmap, make the big bets on where AI can change how people learn, and raise the bar for product thinking across the team. You will work as a thought partner to the leadership team and lead across Product, Engineering, AI/ML, Design, Marketing, Growth and Data.

You will sit at the intersection of learning outcomes, user growth and monetization. Your decisions will directly shape engagement, retention, conversion and LTV for ELSA's consumer business worldwide.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and vision

  • Define and own the multi-year product vision, strategy and roadmap for ELSA's B2C business, tied to clear business goals and learning outcomes

  • Identify and size the biggest growth opportunities across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention and monetization, and make clear bets on where to invest

  • Bring a strong point of view on how AI, LLMs and conversational experiences can change language learning, and turn it into products users love

  • Track market trends, competitors and user behavior to keep ELSA ahead in consumer EdTech and AI learning

Outcomes and metrics

  • Own the B2C North Star and key metrics: activation, DAU/WAU/MAU, engagement, retention, trial and paid conversion, subscription revenue, ARPU, churn and LTV

  • Shape subscription strategy with Growth and Marketing, including pricing, packaging, paywalls, trials and lifecycle engagement

  • Set the measurement framework so every major launch shows a measurable impact on user behavior, learning outcomes and revenue

Product execution at scale

  • Lead the end-to-end consumer experience across onboarding, assessment, personalized learning paths, practice, AI coaching and long-term engagement

  • Drive a culture of high-velocity experimentation, setting the standard for A/B test design, analysis and decision-making across the B2C team

  • Partner with AI/ML on personalization, recommendations, adaptive learning and AI tutor experiences, from early prototype to scaled launch

  • Diagnose the hardest problems in the funnel using deep quantitative and qualitative insight, and turn them into a prioritized plan

Leadership and influence

  • Act as a strategic partner to the executive team, presenting strategy, trade-offs and results clearly

  • Align Engineering, Design, AI/ML, Data, Growth and Marketing around shared goals and priorities

  • Mentor and coach other Product Managers, raising the bar for product discovery, writing, analytics and craft

  • Be the voice of the learner across ELSA, using research, reviews, support feedback and data to guide major decisions

What You Will Have

Must-Haves

  • 10–15 years of product management experience, with at least 5 years in senior roles (Senior, Lead, Group or Principal PM) on B2C digital products, consumer apps, subscription products or other high-scale consumer experiences

  • A track record of owning products at scale (millions of users) with clear, measurable impact on user growth, engagement, retention, conversion or revenue

  • Experience setting product vision and multi-year strategy, not only executing a roadmap

  • Deep expertise in consumer funnels and subscription economics: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention cohorts, conversion, churn, ARPU, CAC and LTV

  • Hands-on, advanced use of product analytics (Amplitude, Mixpanel, GA4, Firebase or similar) and the ability to dig into data yourself

  • Proven experience building an experimentation culture: designing, running and interpreting A/B tests at scale, and making decisions from the results

  • Experience shipping products powered by personalization, recommendations, behavioral data or adaptive experiences

  • Strong leadership and influence without authority, including mentoring PMs and aligning senior cross-functional stakeholders

  • Excellent written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate strategy and trade-offs to executives and the board

  • High ownership: you take responsibility for business and user outcomes, not just delivery

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience leading consumer subscription or freemium mobile apps through a major growth stage, ideally on a global scale across multiple markets

About Parexel


Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insight-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. With 22,000+ employees worldwide, we partner with biopharmaceutical companies and research sites to design and deliver patient-focused clinical trials that broaden access and make research a care option for anyone, anywhere.


We work with focus, agility, and shared purpose, moving with urgency to address patient needs and accelerate the delivery of new therapies. We embrace bold thinking, adapt quickly to change, and continually raise the bar for the speed and quality of clinical research. We are expanding our team and seeking talented individuals to help drive industry-leading innovation, With Heart®.


About the Role


We are seeking a Senior Clinical Research Associate (SCRA) to join our team in Belgium in a remote/home-based capacity.


As a Senior Clinical Research Associate, you will play a critical role in advancing oncology research by ensuring clinical trial quality, data integrity, patient safety, and regulatory compliance at the site level. Working within a sponsor-dedicated model, you will oversee monitoring activities across assigned investigator sites, collaborating closely with site personnel, investigators, and project teams to support successful study delivery.


This position offers the opportunity to contribute directly to the development of innovative therapies while building strong partnerships with sites and stakeholders. You will leverage your expertise in oncology clinical trials, including RECIST criteria, to support study execution through a combination of remote and on-site monitoring activities. Your work will help ensure that studies remain inspection-ready, compliant, and focused on delivering high-quality outcomes for patients.


You will join a collaborative, growth-oriented environment where your contributions are highly visible and where continuous learning, professional development, and meaningful impact are part of everyday work.


Key Responsibilities


  • Ensure compliance with study protocols, ICH-GCP guidelines, regulatory requirements, and company procedures across assigned sites.

  • Verify that informed consent processes are appropriately conducted and documented for each study participant.
  • Assess patient safety and clinical data integrity by identifying protocol deviations, violations, pharmacovigilance concerns, and other site-level risks.

  • Perform source document review and verification, ensuring clinical data entered into case report forms is accurate, complete, and supported by source documentation.

  • Document monitoring findings and study activities through monitoring reports, follow-up letters, communication logs, and other required study documentation.
  • Ensure study activities are performed by appropriately trained and delegated site personnel.
  • Maintain accurate tracking of observations, action items, site status, and study progress within required systems and tracking tools.
  • Review site documentation, training compliance, delegation logs, enrollment logs, accountability records, and other essential study records to ensure ongoing inspection readiness.
  • Participate in investigator meetings, sponsor meetings, monitoring meetings, and project team discussions as required.
  • Collaborate with the primary Site Manager and key stakeholders to support study objectives, deliverables, and timelines.

Candidate Profile

  • Strong networking, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience working within clinical research and regulated environments
  • The ability to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels
  • A patient-focused mindset and commitment to quality, compliance, and data integrity
  • Comfort working with clinical trial systems, monitoring processes, and evolving technologies
  • The flexibility to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining focus on study objectives and timelines

Job Summary:

The Group Leader develops the Group strategy and oversees its implementation, driving high performance and organic growth to ensure the VBU objectives are met across the Education Group. The role supports M&A, participates in due diligence, oversees the integration of acquisitions, ensures Portfolio financial objectives and Volaris metrics are embedded throughout the Group, and ensures business risk management is undertaken consistently.
The Group Leader also drives key initiatives and sets and drives the culture across the Group, ensuring alignment to the broader Education & Cultural Industries Portfolio.

Job Description:

Key duties and responsibilities

1. Strategy and performance

  • Ensure a strategic plan is developed with each VBU and executed so that the key strategic and financial objectives are met across the Group.
  • Meet agreed growth and profitability targets for the Group.
  • Set and then manage the delivery of agreed annual objectives for the Group of companies.
  • Drive the quarterly review process for business and talent performance, ensuring businesses take timely action to address any issues identified.
  • Ensure Group and VBU plans respond to changes in the education market, including curriculum, funding and policy changes.

2. Organic growth, sales and customers

  • Actively engage with VBU Leaders to ensure sales strategy is well aligned to organic growth objectives and that sales channels are focused to generate the expected results.
  • Ensure sales and renewal activity is aligned to academic-year and public-sector budget and procurement cycles.
  • Act as the escalation point for key customer issues within the Group.

3. M&A and integration

  • Participate in M&A activities as required by the Education Portfolio Leader, including participating in meetings with potential targets and undertaking due diligence.
  • Oversee the integration of allocated acquisitions within the Group, ensuring achievement of the integration plan objectives and alignment of IRR for the acquired businesses.
  • Ensure Portfolio financial objectives and Volaris metrics are embedded throughout the Group, including in acquired businesses.
  • Note at this stage the Group Leader role does not have capital deployment targets or responsibilities.

4. People, talent and culture

  • Manage and develop direct reports, including the attraction, retention, development and building of capability and engagement.
  • Ensure adequate talent pipelining, succession planning and talent management to support the growth objectives of the Group, including building capability and engagement within each business in the Group.
  • Ensure structure and resourcing levels enable the Group objectives to be met.
  • Set and drive the culture across the Group, ensuring alignment to the broader Education & Cultural Industries Portfolio.

5. Risk, compliance and governance

  • Oversee business risk management across the Group, including:
    • ensuring compliance and regulatory requirements are met across the Group;
    • ensuring student data privacy and child safeguarding obligations are met (for example GDPR, FERPA, COPPA and the Australian Privacy Act, as relevant);
    • ensuring education products meet accessibility standards (for example WCAG);
    • ensuring risk management strategies are in place to support growth and profitability; and
    • ensuring compliance with all Volaris policies, including cybersecurity policies.

6. Stakeholders

  • Manage strategic internal and external key stakeholder relationships, including education customers, authorities and partners.

7. AI and innovation

  • Drive AI tools adoption and culture evolution across the Group to adopt and exploit AI positively impacting growth, revenue, efficiency and customer retention.
  • Ensure AI is used responsibly in education products, including with regard to academic integrity and student data.

jobs.excerpt: About Acoustic Acoustic is a marketing technology company helping brands build stronger, more lasting relationships with their customers.
jobs.description:
About Acoustic

Acoustic is a marketing technology company helping brands build stronger, more lasting relationships with their customers. Our platform gives marketers a real-time picture of how their audiences behave and what they actually want, so they can show up when it matters most. We believe great marketing feels less like broadcasting and more like listening. That's what we're building.

Our buyers are marketers at consumer brands in retail, travel, and financial services, where a missed moment costs revenue. In this role, you'd sit where our Marketing and Sales teams meet and help us practice what we sell: read the signals our own buyers send, act on them while they matter, and make sure every one reaches the right person with a clear next step.

About the role

As Senior Manager of Go-to-Market Operations, you'll own how buying signals turn into qualified sales opportunities at Acoustic. Reporting to our CMO, you'll bring Marketing and Sales together around one shared funnel, from deciding which accounts to go after and when to reach out to making sure every lead has a clear next step. You'll also be the technical owner of Acoustic Connect for our own marketing team, with room to test how a platform built for B2C customer engagement can support a B2B buying journey and bring what you learn back to the people building it. Day to day, you'll own Qualified, Apollo, and LeanData, partner with the owners of Salesforce and Gong, and build the AI SDRs and agents behind inbound follow-up, outbound prospecting, and internal workflows.

This is a remote role based in the United States.

Requirements

What you'll do

  • Acoustic Connect implementation and adoption: own the configuration, data integrations, audience setup, and automation for Connect at Acoustic, and partner with Marketing to build and measure B2B programs such as lead nurture, event follow-up, and re-engagement. You'll be the internal Connect expert and a direct partner to Product, sharing what works, where marketers hit friction, and which capabilities could open up new ways to use the platform.
  • Intent and account targeting: combine account fit, intent signals, engagement, and conversion data to refine our ideal customer profile and prioritize accounts. Test which signals predict qualified opportunities and use what you learn to improve who we target, when we reach out, and how we follow up.
  • Lead management and sales handoff: own how leads are captured, enriched, scored, routed, and followed up on across inbound and outbound, and set clear rules with Marketing and Sales for who takes the next step, how quickly they act, and when a lead goes back into nurture. Track follow-up coverage, time to first touch, and conversion to qualified opportunity to find and fix gaps in the handoff.
  • AI SDRs and outbound automation: build and manage AI SDRs and agents for inbound qualification, outbound prospecting, follow-up, and internal workflows, and define what each agent handles and when a person steps in. Review outreach quality and use replies, meetings, and opportunity conversion to improve targeting, messaging, and cadences.
  • GTM systems (Qualified, Apollo, LeanData, Salesforce, Gong): own Qualified, Apollo, and LeanData and keep their integrations and workflows running reliably, and partner with the Salesforce and Gong owners to improve data quality and capture lead, account, activity, and opportunity data consistently. Support marketers with campaign tracking, lead capture, and reporting so they can trace programs through to qualified pipeline.
  • Funnel reporting and forecasting: build and maintain one go-to-market funnel model that connects expected demand and outbound activity to pipeline creation and progression. Bring lead volumes, conversion rates, and stage timing into a shared forecast with Marketing and Sales, compare actuals with assumptions, and flag gaps early enough for teams to act.

You could be a great match if

  • Have seven or more years of experience in B2B SaaS go-to-market, revenue, marketing, or sales operations, with hands-on ownership of workflows that connect Marketing and Sales.
  • Have implemented and run a marketing automation or customer engagement platform, including data integrations, audience building, automated journeys, and campaign measurement.
  • Know Salesforce well and have worked with Qualified, Apollo, LeanData, and Gong, or comparable tools for inbound engagement, outbound prospecting, lead routing, and conversation intelligence.
  • Are a hands-on operator. You can get Marketing and Sales aligned on a process, build it yourself, and turn what you learn into specific feedback for Product.
  • Are practical about AI. You've put AI agents or AI SDR workflows into production, and you know how to give an agent a clear job, assess its work, and decide where human judgment matters.
  • Are curious about what makes people respond. You'll dig into a buying signal, a cadence, or a routing rule, and use intent, account, and conversion data to improve targeting and pipeline.
  • Are comfortable with numbers. You can build a forecast from volume, conversion, and timing assumptions, and explain what's driving it, where it's sensitive, and what teams can do about it.

Bonus points if you

  • Have used B2C or commerce-focused platforms that act on real-time behavioral data across channels.

This role may not be a match if

  • You'd rather set strategy than configure systems yourself. This role builds as much as it plans.
  • You prefer a mature stack with established playbooks. Much of this work is building and refining the systems and rules.
  • You'd rather own one function than align Marketing, Sales, and Product around shared rules.
  • You're skeptical of AI agents doing real work. You'll run AI SDRs every day and own the quality of what they send.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Company-sponsored short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) program with company match
  • Flexible PTO: take what you need, when you need it
  • Parental leave: 16 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents

  • Strong leadership and management skills, including team development, coaching, performance management, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Proven ability to lead change management initiatives, standardize workflows, implement process improvements, and support technology adoption across revenue cycle operations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify implementation risks, evaluate operational impacts, troubleshoot system issues, and develop effective solutions.
  • Experience developing and monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs), project dashboards, implementation milestones, quality assurance measures, and operational performance reporting.

jobs.description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line.

With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.

This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.

What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor.

Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones. At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

The team

You join an 8-person puzzle studio in Istanbul, founded by Peak and Zynga alumni. It's backed by Homa's puzzle, data, art, and UA teams. Its new puzzle game is heading to global launch, and fresh levels are now its biggest growth lever.

The opportunity

You own the levels players see every week. You work every day with Homa's product director and the studio's level designers, artists, and engineers. You use a level editor and AI tools that generate layouts and estimate difficulty. AI makes you faster, and you stay the brain behind every level. You work remotely from Türkiye. The team is small, and the bar is high.

As the studio grows, you can own a family of mechanics or a pack of levels. You can also lead a group of level designers, or move toward a product role.

Your responsibilities

  • Build. Your levels keep fresh content reaching players, every single week.
  • Tune. Your difficulty curve makes levels feel hard but fair, so players keep trying.
  • Introduce. New mechanics land smoothly because your levels teach them step by step.
  • Test. You play every level before release, so players only see levels that work.
  • Optimize. You use win rate, attempts and churn data to turn weak live levels into strong ones.
  • Shape. Your ideas on new mechanics and content push the game forward.
  • Accelerate. You use AI to generate layout variants, explore difficulty options and check solvability.

What we look for

  • Ownership. You drive outcomes. When something breaks, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke.
  • Proactive. You don't wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it.
  • Pragmatism. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship.
  • AI-driven. AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink.
  • Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly.
  • Motivated. You're ambitious and grounded. You see this opportunity as a chance to learn faster than anywhere else.

Requirements

  • Experience. 1+ year in level design, game design or QA on mobile games, ideally puzzle games.
  • Languages. Fluent Turkish and English. You use both every day.
  • Volume with quality. You ship every week and never let quality slip.
  • Tool speed. You work fast in a level editor and pick up new tools quickly.
  • Data sense. You track level data and use it to tune your levels.
  • Puzzle instinct. You play puzzle games a lot and can explain why a level works.
  • AI native. You turn AI into output. You've built tools that generate layouts, check solvability or analyse level data.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Shipped levels on a live mobile puzzle game.
  • Experience with Unity or a similar game engine.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Our process (2 weeks max)

  • Call with our recruiter (30 min). A generalized conversation, and to tell you more about the role.
  • Level design case study. We look at your thinking and your technical skills.
  • Technical interview with the studio's level designers to dive deeper into technicalities.
  • Final interview with the studio founder and Homa's Puzzle lead. Focused on motivation, values, and fit.

Benefits

Why Homa

  • Exceptional growth. We hire people of outstanding potential, then put them where they can grow fastest. Your scope and your rewards grow with what you deliver, not with tenure.
  • Real ownership. No layers between you and the result. You own outcomes, not tasks, whatever your level.
  • Direct impact. Your work moves the business and shapes where Homa goes next. Decisions are made fast, and you see the results in the numbers.
  • AI at the core. With access to the best AI tools, you'll help shape how an AI-first company works, and your time goes where your judgment matters most.
  • High talent bar. Our teams are small, with people from the best companies, and the talent around you will push you to grow.

What we offer

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here's what you can expect:

  • Comprehensive benefits. Depending on where you're based, you'll get perks such as health insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym membership, and more.
  • A brand-new Paris HQ. A desk in our new office in the heart of Paris, whenever you want to work side by side with the team.
  • An international team. Work in English with top talent from 35+ countries across Europe, the UK, the US, and beyond. Our diversity fuels our creativity.
  • Team gatherings. We value time together beyond the screen. Join regular team gatherings and off-site retreats to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
  • Performance reviews. Every six months, we look back at your progress, recognise your wins, and agree on clear goals for what's next.
  • Equipment support. From day one, you get everything you need to do your best work, including a home office allowance if you work remotely.

Where we hire

Our Paris HQ is a lively hub for creativity, collaboration, and connection. From lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, it's a space people genuinely enjoy, in our brand-new office in the heart of Paris (awesome energy and snacks included).

We also have great teammates across Europe, from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. Whether you work from home in Barcelona or Warsaw, you're fully part of our culture. To keep collaboration smooth, we mainly hire within European time zones (UTC to UTC+3). If you're based there, or planning to be, we'd love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Accenture Song Service helps leading brands turn customer interactions into an engine for growth, moving service beyond a cost center to something that builds trust, loyalty, and share of wallet. Our Service practice works end to end: we shape the vision and strategy for the service function and help clients implement and run it, innovate the products and services customers rely on, equip client customer service and customer experience teams with the right technology and talent, and turn customer data into insights that strengthen client’s relationship with their customers.


Service AI & Data puts AI at the heart of this work. We help clients reinvent how they serve their customers and support their people: conversational AI and AI agents that resolve customer needs across voice, chat, and messaging; copilots that help service agents and field teams do their best work; and the data foundations, data lakes, reporting, and analytics agents that turn every interaction into insight. The strategies we shape and the experiences we design are delivered into production at enterprise scale.


Who you are:

You are an AI Value Engineer who bridges the gap between business need and AI build in customer service. You identify where AI can create real value in a client's service operation, quantify it in terms leaders care about, and track the value AI initiatives create long after launch, so clients can see exactly what their investment is returning. You are equally at home building a value model, facilitating a stakeholder workshop, and shaping a rapid prototype.


You bring a commercial, outcome-driven mindset to everything you do. You ask sharp questions, challenge assumptions with data, and explain tradeoffs in plain language to client leaders and engineers alike. You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, moving between engagements and picking up new domains quickly. Above all, you are a curious, collaborative teammate who makes the people around you better.


The work:

  • Embed with client service and business teams to understand how their service operation creates and loses value, from contact volumes and drivers to agent workflows, operating costs, and customer outcomes.
  • Identify and quantify AI value hypotheses, analyzing contact drivers, interaction data, and operational metrics to find where AI can improve containment, handle time, first-contact resolution, CSAT, retention, and cost-to-serve.
  • Run use-case discovery and prioritization workshops with client stakeholders, mapping use cases against value, feasibility, and risk to build a prioritized AI roadmap.
  • Build business cases and ROI models that client leaders can trust and defend, including baselines, benefit assumptions, build and run costs, and sensitivity analysis.
  • Run cost-benefit and scenario analyses to identify the best solution, comparing options such as build versus buy, platform and model choices, levels of automation, and phased rollouts, and making the tradeoffs behind each one clear.
  • Build the full cost of AI into the business case, including run costs such as token usage, inference, and platform fees, how those costs scale with volume, and the human oversight AI solutions still need, such as review and escalations, so clients can see the true cost per interaction of each option.
  • Map value to specific build initiatives, translating each prioritized use case into scope, success metrics, and requirements that Forward Deployed Engineers and AI Solution Engineering teams can build against.
  • Define service scorecards with client leaders, selecting and prioritizing the KPIs that matter most for their business goals, such as lowering cost-to-serve, improving customer experience, or retaining revenue, and balancing efficiency metrics like containment and handle time against quality metrics like resolution, CSAT, and customer effort, so AI is never optimized for one at the expense of the other.
  • Define how value will be measured before a build begins, setting baselines, KPIs, and measurement plans, and using control groups or A/B tests to attribute impact to the AI solution rather than other factors.
  • Track the value AI initiatives create over time, creating and maintaining value dashboards and benefits tracking across a client's portfolio of AI use cases. Pull data from client data warehouses and data lakes using SQL or Python to validate savings and results against the business case.
  • Run regular value reviews with client business, finance, and service leaders, reporting realized versus planned value, flagging early when an initiative is off track, and recommending what to fix, scale, or stop.
  • Feed realized value back into the roadmap, so the next round of AI investment is prioritized by proven results rather than projections.
  • Tell the story with data, designing clear visualizations, dashboards, and executive-ready presentations that turn complex analysis into a simple narrative: where value is, what it is worth, and what to do next, so clients can make confident investment decisions.
  • Contribute reusable value models, benchmarks, and use-case libraries from the field so our teams can size and prove value faster on the next engagement.
  • Help onboard and mentor junior teammates, and contribute to project debriefs and team POVs.

Here's what you'll need:

  • 3+ years of professional experience in management or technology consulting, business analysis, value engineering, product management, or customer service operations and analytics.
  • 3+ years of experience working on customer service, contact center, or customer experience projects or operations, with a strong command of service metrics such as containment, first-contact resolution, average handle time, CSAT, and cost-to-serve, and their financial impact. Experience should include:
    • Experience building business cases, ROI models, and value measurement frameworks for technology or AI initiatives, and tracking realized value after launch.
    • Experience defining service scorecards or KPI frameworks and prioritizing metrics based on business needs.
    • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets, including cost-benefit and scenario analysis.
    • Hands-on SQL skills to pull and analyze data from data warehouses and data lakes (Python is a plus), and experience with a BI tool such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker.
    • Strong data visualization and storytelling skills, with the ability to choose the right visual for the message and build a clear, compelling narrative from data for executive audiences.
    • A working understanding of AI and LLM capabilities, limits, and cost drivers, such as token usage, model choice, and inference volume, enough to assess feasibility, compare AI and human cost per interaction, and challenge assumptions about what AI can deliver.
    • Familiarity with enterprise AI platforms on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to client locations.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience with contact center analytics, such as contact driver and intent analysis, speech and interaction analytics, or workforce management data.
  • Experience designing experiments, such as A/B tests and control groups, to measure business impact.
  • Experience with benefits realization or value tracking practices, including working with client finance teams to validate savings and returns.
  • Experience with customer service platforms.
  • A portfolio of business cases, value models, or prototypes you can walk us through.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, economics, engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

About the role:

As a Field Service Engineer at Boston Scientific, you will serve as a trusted technical partner to our customers by installing, maintaining, and servicing Boston Scientific medical systems and devices. This is a hands-on, field-based role that requires strong technical expertise and the ability to solve problems independently.

This position plays a critical role in ensuring customer satisfaction through a consistent commitment to delivering high-quality service. You will manage your own territory and work closely with healthcare providers and patients to support optimal equipment performance, user training, and overall service delivery.

This role supports Boston Scientific’s Cardiovascular Division, including products such as IVUS, AVVIGO, AngioJet, ICEfx, FARAPULSE, Rhythmia, and SmartFreeze systems.

Collaboration with cross-functional teams may include support for sales, complaint resolution, event coverage, and field documentation, depending on business needs.

The selected candidate will reside in/near Houston, TX and provide coverage to the Central Region of the U.S. as needed. This position offers a high level of independence, with support and collaboration from senior team members as required.

Interested in hearing directly from a Field Service Engineer at Boston Scientific? Check out our video featuring Bob to learn more about the role:

Work model, sponsorship, relocation:

This is a remote, field-based position. The selected candidate will work primarily at customer locations throughout the assigned territory and from a home-based office when not traveling.

Boston Scientific will not offer sponsorship or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for this position at this time.

Relocation assistance of $5,000 is available for out-of-state candidates.

      • Completion of a biomedical equipment technician (BMET) certification, formal technical training program, or military technical training with a minimum of 1 year of hands-on experience

Leap Event Technology is a remote-friendly company. This position is open to any candidate in North America.

Leap is revolutionizing the event technology industry by empowering organizers to create experiences that are more engaging, more thrilling, and more impactful than ever before. With offices in Dallas, Montreal, and Sydney, and an expansive remote workforce across the globe, our diverse backgrounds give us the experience needed to create incredible events for any industry, anywhere in the world.

Sounds interesting? Let’s talk.

Leap is hiring a Senior Director of Data and Analytics to lead the Data and Analytics teams within Leap Marketing & Analytics (LMA). This leader owns our data and analytics strategy, runs our data platform and turns it into fan intelligence and executive dashboards our clients rely on. Data is the product at LMA. Team leadership

  • Hire, mentor and grow data engineers, analysts and BI developers

Data platform

  • Build and maintain pipelines from ticketing, CRM and messaging platforms, plus third party data appends
  • Enforce standards for data quality, documentation and client data privacy

Executive dashboards and fan intelligence

  • Lead the design and delivery of executive dashboards in Omni, Tableau and Power BI
  • Turn fan, ticketing and engagement data into audience segments, propensity models and revenue insights

AI-driven analytics

Clients

Strategy and business ownership

  • Own the data and analytics strategy and roadmap with Joe
  • Own the business results and P&L impact of LMA's data services
  • Act as the senior data voice in executive client meetings and new business pitches

What you bring

  • 12+ years in data engineering, analytics or business intelligence
  • 5+ years managing data or analytics teams, including managing managers Hands-on experience with Snowflake or a similar cloud data warehouse, ideally on AWS
  • A portfolio of executive dashboards in Omni, Tableau or Power BI that leaders used to make decisions
  • Experience with fan, audience or customer analytics, ideally in sports, live events, entertainment or ticketing
  • Strong SQL and data modeling skills; Python a plus
  • Working knowledge of CRM and marketing platforms as data sources (Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Klaviyo) Practical experience applying generative AI to analytics work
  • Ability to explain data clearly to executives and clients

Nice to have

  • Experience with identity resolution and third-party data appends
  • Agency or client-services experience

BENEFITS:

We offer

Leap Event Technology is a remote-friendly company. However, we do offer the option of working in the office for employees located in Montréal (CAN), Pittsburgh (U.S.), Dallas (U.S.), Sydney (AUS).
